title.zh: 卷三百三十七 列傳第九十六 范鎮從子:百祿 從孫:祖禹
title.en: Volume 337 Biographies 96: Fan Zhen and Newpher: Bailu, Relative: Zuyu
title.raw: 卷三百三十七 列傳第九十六 范鎮從子:百祿 從孫:祖禹 Volume 337 Biographies 96: Fan Zhen and Newpher: Bailu, Relative: Zuyu

sentences.zh: 范鎮，字景仁，成都華陽人。

translations.literal: Fan Zhen, styled Jingren, was a man of Huayang in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen, whose style was Jingren, came from Huayang in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 薛奎守蜀，一見愛之，館於府舍，俾與子弟講學。

translations.literal: When Xue Kui guarded Shu, at first sight he loved him, lodged him in the prefectural residence, and had him lecture and study with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as prefect of Shu, Xue Kui took an immediate liking to him, housed him in the government compound, and had him study alongside his own sons.

sentences.zh: 鎮益自謙退，每步行趨府門，逾年，人不知其為帥客也。

translations.literal: Zhen became even more modest and retiring; each time he walked hastening to the prefectural gate; after more than a year people did not know he was the commander's guest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen grew still more humble and unassuming, walking on foot to the prefect's gate each day; after more than a year, no one even knew he was the prefect's guest.

sentences.zh: 及還朝，載以俱。

translations.literal: When he returned to court, he took him along together.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue returned to the capital, he brought Zhen with him.

sentences.zh: 有問奎入蜀何所得，曰：「得一偉人，當以文學名世。」

translations.literal: When someone asked what Kui had gained from entering Shu, he said: "I gained one great man who will make a name for himself in letters."
translations.idiomatic: Asked what he had gained from his tour in Shu, Xue replied, "I found one extraordinary man who will win fame through literature."

sentences.zh: 宋庠兄弟見其文，自謂弗及，與為布衣交。

translations.literal: The Song Qi brothers saw his writings, said themselves they could not match him, and became friends with him as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song Qi brothers read his work, they admitted they could not equal him and befriended him as equals, without regard to rank.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，禮部奏名第一。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; the Ministry of Rites reported his name first.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination and ranked first on the Ministry of Rites list.

sentences.zh: 故事，殿廷唱第過三人，則首禮部選者，必越次抗聲自陳，率得置上列。

translations.literal: By precedent, when more than three names had been announced in the palace for graduates, the top Ministry of Rites selection would step out of order and loudly state his case, and usually was placed in the upper row.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, once three names had been called in the palace examination, the top candidate from the Ministry of Rites list would step forward out of turn and protest loudly, and was usually placed in a higher rank.

sentences.zh: 吳育、歐陽修號稱耿介，亦從眾。

translations.literal: Wu Yu and Ouyang Xiu were styled upright and unyielding, yet they too followed the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yu and Ouyang Xiu, renowned for their integrity, followed the crowd as well.

sentences.zh: 鎮獨不然，同列屢趣之，不為動。

translations.literal: Zhen alone was not so; those in the same row repeatedly urged him, but he was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen alone refused; his fellows in the row urged him again and again, but he would not budge.

sentences.zh: 至第七十九人，乃從呼出應，退就列，無一言，廷中皆異之。

translations.literal: Only when the seventy-ninth person was called did he then follow the call and respond, withdrew to his row, and uttered not a word; all in the court were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the seventy-ninth name was called did he step forward to answer, then returned to his place without a word; the entire court was astonished.

sentences.zh: 自是舊風遂革。

translations.literal: From then on the old practice was reformed.
translations.idiomatic: From that day forward, the old custom was abolished.

sentences.zh: 調新安主簿，西京留守宋綬延置國子監，薦為東監直講。

translations.literal: He was assigned recorder of Xin'an; the Western Capital intendant Song Shou extended invitation and placed him in the Directorate of Education, recommending him as Eastern Supervisor Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned as registrar of Xin'an, he was brought into the Directorate of Education by the Western Capital intendant Song Shou, who recommended him as Eastern Supervisor Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 召試學士院，當得館閣校理，主司妄以為失韻，補校勘。

translations.literal: Summoned to the Academy examination, he should have received Hanlin collation; the chief examiner wrongly deemed his rhyme faulty and gave him proofreader instead.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the Hanlin examination, he should have received a collation post in the archives; the chief examiner wrongly judged his rhymes defective and appointed him proofreader instead.

sentences.zh: 人為忿鬱，而鎮處之晏如。

translations.literal: People were angry and distressed for him, but Zhen took it calmly.
translations.idiomatic: Others were indignant on his behalf, but Zhen remained perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 經四年，當遷，宰相龐籍言：「鎮有異材，不汲汲於進取。」

translations.literal: After four years, when he was due for promotion, Grand Councilor Pang Ji said: "Zhen has unusual talent and is not anxious about advancement."
translations.idiomatic: After four years, when he was due for promotion, Grand Councilor Pang Ji remarked, "Zhen possesses extraordinary ability and is not eager for advancement."

sentences.zh: 超授直秘閣，判吏部南曹、開封府推官。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Direct Gentleman of the Secret Archive, and concurrently judged the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel and served as investigating official of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to Direct Gentleman of the Secret Archive and concurrently assigned to the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel and as investigating official of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 擢起居舍人、知諫院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant on the Grand Secretariat and put in charge of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant on the Grand Secretariat and placed in charge of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 上疏論：「民力困敝，請約祖宗以來官吏兵數，酌取其中為定制，以今賦入之數什七為經費，儲其三以備水旱非常。」

translations.literal: He memorialized arguing: "The people's strength is exhausted and worn. I ask that the numbers of officials and troops since the founding ancestors be reviewed, a median taken as a fixed regulation, that seventy percent of current tax receipts be used as operating expenses, and the remaining three-tenths stored against flood, drought, and emergencies."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he argued, "The people's strength is exhausted and worn. I ask that the numbers of officials and troops since the founding ancestors be reviewed, a median taken as a fixed regulation, that seventy percent of current tax receipts be used as operating expenses, and the remaining three-tenths stored against flood, drought, and emergencies."

sentences.zh: 又言：「周以冢宰制國用，唐以宰相判鹽鐵、度支。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Zhou used the chief steward to control state expenditures; the Tang had the chief minister oversee Salt Iron and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "The Zhou entrusted state finances to the chief steward; the Tang had the chief minister oversee the Salt Iron and Revenue bureaus.

sentences.zh: 今中書主民，樞密主兵，三司主財，各不相知。

translations.literal: Today the Secretariat controls the people, the Military Affairs Commission controls troops, and the Salt Iron Commission controls finances, and each does not know the others.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Secretariat governs the people, the Military Affairs Commission commands the army, and the Salt Iron Commission manages finances, yet none coordinates with the others.

sentences.zh: 財已匱，樞密益兵無窮；

translations.literal: Finances are already depleted, yet the Commission endlessly increases troops;
translations.idiomatic: Treasury funds are already exhausted, yet the Military Affairs Commission endlessly expands the army;

sentences.zh: 民已困，三司取財不已。

translations.literal: the people are already distressed, yet the Commission ceaselessly extracts wealth.
translations.idiomatic: the people are already impoverished, yet the Salt Iron Commission never stops extracting revenue.

sentences.zh: 請使二府通知兵民大計，與三司同制國用。」

translations.literal: I ask that the two commissions be made aware of the great plans for troops and people jointly with the Salt Iron Commission to control state expenditures."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the two commissions be informed of the grand strategy for troops and people and jointly with the Salt Iron Commission control state expenditures."

sentences.zh: 契丹使至，虛聲示強，大臣益募兵以塞責，歲費百千萬。

translations.literal: When Khitan envoys arrived and blustered to show strength, grand ministers increased recruitment to meet their responsibility, costing millions each year.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan envoys arrived boasting of their strength, grand ministers stepped up recruitment to meet their obligations, costing millions each year.

sentences.zh: 鎮言：「備契丹莫若寬三晉之民，備靈夏莫若寬秦民，備西南莫若寬越、蜀之民，備天下莫若寬天下之民。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "To guard against the Khitan, nothing is better than easing the people of the Three Jin; against Ling and Xia, easing the people of Qin; against the southwest, easing the people of Yue and Shu; to guard the realm, easing the people under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "The best defense against the Khitan is to lighten the burden on the people of the Three Jin; against Ling and Xia, ease the plight of the Qin people; against the southwest, relieve the people of Yue and Shu; to secure the realm, lighten the burden on all the people under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 夫兵所以衛民而反殘民，臣恐異日之憂不在四夷，而在冗兵與窮民也。」

translations.literal: Troops exist to protect the people yet in fact harm them; I fear that future troubles will lie not with the four barbarians but with redundant troops and destitute people."
translations.idiomatic: Armies exist to protect the people, yet they end up harming them instead. I fear that future troubles will stem not from the four barbarian frontiers but from bloated armies and impoverished commoners."

sentences.zh: 商人輸粟河北，取償京師，而榷貨不即予鈔，久而鬻之，十才得其六。

translations.literal: Merchants shipped grain to Hebei to receive payment in the capital, but monopoly goods were not promptly issued with vouchers; after long delays when sold they recovered only six-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants shipped grain to Hebei to receive payment in the capital, but monopoly goods were not promptly exchanged for vouchers; after long delays when they sold them, they recovered only sixty percent of their value.

sentences.zh: 或建議出內帑錢，稍增價與市，歲可得羡息五十萬。

translations.literal: Some proposed drawing from the inner treasury to buy at slightly raised prices, yielding fifty thousand in annual surplus interest.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed using funds from the inner treasury to buy at slightly higher prices, yielding five hundred thousand in annual surplus profit.

sentences.zh: 鎮謂：「外府內帑，均為有司。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "The outer offices and the inner treasury alike belong to the fiscal authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen objected, "The outer offices and the inner treasury alike belong to the fiscal authorities.

sentences.zh: 今使外府滯商人，而內帑乘急以牟利，至傷國體。」

translations.literal: Now to let the outer offices hold up merchants while the inner treasury profiteers in their distress damages the integrity of the state."
translations.idiomatic: To let the outer offices hold merchants in limbo while the inner treasury profits from their distress damages the dignity of the state."

sentences.zh: 仁宗遽止之。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong immediately stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong immediately halted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 葬溫成后，太常議禮，前謂之園，後謂之陵，宰相劉沆前為監護使，後為園陵使。

translations.literal: When Empress Wencheng was buried, the Directorate of Sacrifices debated ritual: first they called it a park, later a mausoleum; Chief Councilor Liu Hang first served as supervisor of the burial, later as park-and-mausoleum commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial of Empress Wencheng, the Directorate of Sacrifices debated the rites: first calling the site a park, later a mausoleum; Chief Councilor Liu Hang first served as burial supervisor, then as park-and-mausoleum commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鎮曰：「嘗聞法吏舞法矣，未聞禮官舞禮也。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "I have heard of law officers twisting the law, but never of ritual officers twisting ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "I have heard of law officers twisting the law, but never of ritual officers twisting ritual.

sentences.zh: 請詰前後議禮異同狀。」

translations.literal: I request an inquiry into the discrepancy between the earlier and later ritual deliberations."
translations.idiomatic: I request an inquiry into why the ritual deliberations differed before and after."

sentences.zh: 集賢校理刁約論壙中物侈麗，吳充、鞠真卿爭論禮，並補外，皆上章留之。

translations.literal: Collation Official Diao Yue criticized luxury in the tomb chamber goods; Wu Chong and Ju Zhenqing disputed ritual; all were posted outside the capital; each submitted memorials to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Collation Official Diao Yue criticized the extravagance of the tomb furnishings; Wu Chong and Ju Zhenqing disputed the rites; all were reassigned to posts outside the capital, and each submitted a memorial asking to remain.

sentences.zh: 石全贇護葬，轉觀察使，他吏悉優遷兩官，鎮言：「章獻、章懿、章惠三后之葬，推恩皆無此比。

translations.literal: Shi Quanyun supervised the burial and was transferred to observation commissioner; other officials all received two-rank preferential advancement. Zhen said: "At the burials of the three empresses Zhangxian, Zhangyi, and Zhanghui, largesse had no such parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Quanyun, who supervised the burial, was promoted to observation commissioner, and all other officials received preferential advancement of two ranks. Zhen said, "At the burials of Empresses Zhangxian, Zhangyi, and Zhanghui, no such largesse was ever granted.

sentences.zh: 乞追還全贇等告敕。」

translations.literal: I beg that the patents for Quanyun and others be recalled."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the patents for Quanyun and the others be recalled."

sentences.zh: 副都知任守忠、鄧保吉同日除官，內臣無故改官者又五六人。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service Ren Shouzhong and Deng Baoji were promoted on the same day, and five or six more eunuchs were promoted without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Ren Shouzhong and Deng Baoji were promoted on the same day, and five or six more eunuchs were given new offices without cause.

sentences.zh: 時有敕，凡內降非準律令者，並許執奏。

translations.literal: There was then an edict that whenever inner decrees not conforming to statutes and ordinances were issued, memorials opposing them were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had just been issued permitting officials to memorialize against any inner decree that did not conform to statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 曾未一月，大臣輒廢不行。

translations.literal: Before a month had passed the grand ministers set it aside and did not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Before a month had passed, the grand ministers set the edict aside and refused to enforce it.

sentences.zh: 鎮乞正中書、樞密之罪，以示天下。

translations.literal: Zhen asked that the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission be punished to show the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen asked that the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission be punished to set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝天性寬仁，言事者競為激訐，至污人以帷箔不可明之事。

translations.literal: The emperor was by nature lenient and humane; those who spoke on affairs vied in harsh criticism, even smearing people with affairs behind curtains that could not be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was by nature lenient and humane, yet those who spoke on affairs vied in harsh denunciation, even smearing opponents with scandalous private matters that could not be verified.

sentences.zh: 鎮獨務引大體，非關朝廷安危，生民利疚，則闊略不言。

translations.literal: Zhen alone kept to the larger pattern; unless it concerned the court's safety or the people's welfare, he broadly omitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen alone kept to the larger principles; unless a matter touched the court's safety or the people's welfare, he passed over it in silence.

sentences.zh: 陳執中為相，鎮論其無學術，非宰相器。

translations.literal: When Chen Zhizhong became chief councilor, Zhen argued he lacked learning and was no material for chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Zhizhong became chief councilor, Zhen argued that he lacked learning and was unfit for the post.

sentences.zh: 及嬖妾笞殺婢，御史劾奏，欲逐去之。

translations.literal: When his favorite concubine beat a maid to death, the censorate impeached him and sought to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: When his favorite concubine beat a maid to death, the censorate impeached him and sought his removal.

sentences.zh: 鎮言：「今陰陽不和，財匱民困，盜賊滋熾，獄犴充斥，執中當任其咎。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Now yin and yang are discordant, finances are exhausted and the people distressed, bandits multiply, and prisons overflow; Zhizhong should bear the blame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "Heaven and earth are out of harmony, the treasury is empty and the people suffer, banditry flourishes, and the prisons overflow—Zhizhong should bear the blame for all of this.

sentences.zh: 御史舍大責細，暴揚燕私，若用此為進退，是因一婢逐宰相，非所以明等級，辨堂陛。」

translations.literal: The censorate abandons the great charge for the small, exposing private household matters; if this were used for dismissal and appointment, it would be driving out a chief councilor over one maid—not how to clarify grades and distinguish hall from steps."
translations.idiomatic: The censorate abandons the weighty charge for a trivial one, exposing private household affairs; if this were grounds for dismissal, it would mean driving out a chief councilor over a single maid—not how to clarify ranks and distinguish the hall from the steps."

sentences.zh: 識者韙之。

translations.literal: The knowing approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood the matter approved his view.

sentences.zh: 文彥博、富弼入相，詔百官郊迎。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi entered as chief councilors; an edict ordered all officials to greet them at the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi became chief councilors, an edict ordered all officials to greet them at the suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 鎮曰：「隆之以虛禮，不若推之以至誠。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "To honor them with empty ceremony is not as good as advancing them with utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "Honoring them with empty ceremony is not as good as advancing them with utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 陛下用兩人為相，舉朝皆謂得人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty employs these two men as chief councilors; the whole court says you have gained the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has appointed these two men as chief councilors, and the entire court agrees you have chosen well.

sentences.zh: 然近制，兩制不得詣宰相居第，百官不得間見，是不推之以誠也。

translations.literal: Yet recent regulations forbid drafted officials to visit the chief councilors' residences and forbid officials generally to see them in private—that is not advancing them in sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet recent regulations forbid drafted officials to visit the chief councilors at home and forbid other officials private access—that is not treating them with sincerity.

sentences.zh: 願罷郊迎，除謁禁，則於御臣之術為兩得矣。」

translations.literal: I wish the suburban greeting be abolished and visitation prohibitions lifted; then in the art of steering ministers both aims would be gained."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the suburban greeting be abolished and visitation restrictions lifted; then in the art of governing ministers both aims would be served."

sentences.zh: 議減任子及每歲取士，皆自鎮發之。

translations.literal: Deliberations to reduce hereditary privilege and annual recruitment of degree holders all began from Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberations to reduce hereditary privilege and limit annual recruitment of degree holders all originated with Zhen.

sentences.zh: 又乞令宗室疏屬補外官，帝曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: He also asked that distant collateral of the imperial clan be assigned outer posts; the emperor said: "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that distant collateral members of the imperial clan be assigned posts outside the capital; the emperor said, "Your words are right.

sentences.zh: 顧恐天下謂朕不能睦族耳。」

translations.literal: Only I fear the realm will say I cannot treat my kin with kindness."
translations.idiomatic: Only I fear the realm will say I cannot treat my own kin with kindness."

sentences.zh: 鎮曰：「陛下甄別其賢者用之，不沒其能，乃所以睦族也。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Your Majesty selects the worthy among them for use and does not bury their ability—that is how to treat kin with kindness."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "Your Majesty selects the worthy among them for office and does not suppress their abilities—that is how to treat your kin with kindness."

sentences.zh: 雖不行，至熙寧初，卒如其言。

translations.literal: Though not adopted then, by the beginning of Xining it was finally done as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Though not adopted at the time, by the beginning of the Xining era it was finally carried out as he had urged.

sentences.zh: 帝在位三十五年，未有繼嗣。

translations.literal: The emperor had reigned thirty-five years without an heir.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had reigned thirty-five years without an heir.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐初，暴得疾，中外大小之臣，無不寒心，莫敢先言者，鎮獨奮曰：「天下事尚有大於此者乎？」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiayou he suddenly fell ill; officials great and small within and without were heartsick and none dared speak first; Zhen alone roused himself and said: "Is there any matter under Heaven greater than this?"
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiayou era the emperor suddenly fell ill; officials great and small, at court and beyond, were heartsick, and none dared speak first. Zhen alone roused himself and declared, "Is there any matter under Heaven greater than this?"

sentences.zh: 即拜疏曰：「置諫官者，為宗廟社稷計。

translations.literal: He immediately submitted a memorial: "Remonstrance officials are appointed for the ancestral temples and altars.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a memorial: "Remonstrance officials are appointed for the sake of the ancestral temples and the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 諫官而不以宗廟社稷計事陛下，是愛死嗜利之人，臣不為也。

translations.literal: A remonstrance officer who does not take the temples and altars into account in serving Your Majesty is one who clings to life and craves profit; I will not be such a man.
translations.idiomatic: A remonstrance officer who does not take the temples and altars into account when serving Your Majesty is a man who clings to life and craves profit—and I will not be such a man.

sentences.zh: 方陛下不豫，海內皇皇莫知所為，陛下獨以祖宗後裔為念，是為宗廟之慮，至深且明也。

translations.literal: While Your Majesty was unwell, within the seas all were anxious and none knew what to do; Your Majesty alone thought of the descendants of the ancestors—that is consideration for the temples, most deep and clear.
translations.idiomatic: While Your Majesty was unwell, the realm was in turmoil and no one knew what to do; Your Majesty alone thought of the descendants of the ancestors—that is consideration for the temples, profound and clear.

sentences.zh: 昔太祖舍其子而立太宗，天下之大公也。

translations.literal: Formerly Taizu set aside his son and established Taizong—that was the great public interest of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Taizu set aside his own son and established Taizong—that was the great public interest of the realm.

sentences.zh: 真宗以周王薨，養宗子於宮中，天下之大慮也。

translations.literal: Zhenzong, when Prince of Zhou died, raised an imperial clansman in the palace—that was the great prudent concern of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Zhou died, Zhenzong raised an imperial clansman in the palace—that was the great prudent concern of the realm.

sentences.zh: 願以太祖之心，行真宗故事，拔近屬之尤賢者，優其禮秩，置之左右，與圖天下事，以繫億兆人心。」

translations.literal: I wish that with Taizu's heart Your Majesty follow Zhenzong's precedent, select the most worthy among close kin, enhance their ritual rank, place them at Your side to plan realm affairs, and thereby bind the hearts of the hundred millions."
translations.idiomatic: I wish that with Taizu's spirit Your Majesty follow Zhenzong's precedent, select the worthiest among close kin, honor them with high rank, place them at Your side to plan the affairs of the realm, and thereby bind the hearts of the hundred millions."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，文彥博使客問何所言，以實告，客曰：「如是，何不與執政謀？」

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Wen Yanbo sent a client to ask what he had said; told truthfully, the client said: "If so, why not consult the chief councilors first?"
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Wen Yanbo sent an emissary to ask what he had written; told the truth, the emissary said, "If that is so, why not consult the chief councilors first?"

sentences.zh: 鎮曰：「自分必死，故敢言。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "I counted myself sure to die, therefore I dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "I counted myself as good as dead, and therefore I dared speak.

sentences.zh: 若謀於執政，或以為不可，豈得中輟乎？」

translations.literal: If I had consulted the chief councilors and they thought it impossible, could I have stopped halfway?"
translations.idiomatic: If I had consulted the chief councilors and they judged it impossible, could I have stopped halfway?"

sentences.zh: 章累上，不報。

translations.literal: Memorials piled up without response.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials piled up without response.

sentences.zh: 執政諭之曰：「奈何效希名干進之人。」

translations.literal: The chief councilors instructed him: "Why imitate men who crave reputation and angle for advancement?"
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilors admonished him, "Why imitate men who crave reputation and angle for advancement?"

sentences.zh: 鎮貽以書曰：「比天象見變，當有急兵，鎮義當死職，不可死亂兵之下。

translations.literal: Zhen sent a letter: "Recently celestial phenomena showed change; there will surely be urgent military troubles. Zhen's duty is to die in office; he cannot die under mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen sent a letter in reply: "Recently celestial omens showed change; urgent military troubles are surely coming. My duty is to die in office—I cannot die beneath mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 此乃鎮擇死之時，尚何顧希名干進之嫌哉？」

translations.literal: This is the time Zhen chooses to die; what need to worry about the suspicion of craving renown and advancement?"
translations.idiomatic: This is the time I choose to die—what need is there to worry about the suspicion of craving fame and advancement?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下得臣疏，不以留中而付中書，是欲使大臣奉行也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your Majesty received my memorial and did not retain it but handed it to the Secretariat—that means you wish the grand ministers to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Your Majesty received my memorial and did not retain it but forwarded it to the Secretariat—that means you wish the grand ministers to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 臣兩至中書，大臣皆設辭拒臣，是陛下欲為宗廟社稷計，而大臣不欲也。

translations.literal: Twice I went to the Secretariat; the grand ministers all made excuses and refused me—Your Majesty wishes to plan for the temples but the grand ministers do not.
translations.idiomatic: Twice I went to the Secretariat, and the grand ministers all made excuses and refused me—Your Majesty wishes to plan for the temples and altars, but the grand ministers do not.

sentences.zh: 臣竊原大臣畏避之意，恐行之而陛下中變耳。

translations.literal: I privately surmise the grand ministers' intent in holding back: they fear carrying it out while Your Majesty changes your mind midway.
translations.idiomatic: I privately surmise why the grand ministers hold back: they fear carrying it out while Your Majesty changes your mind midway.

sentences.zh: 中變之禍，不過一死。

translations.literal: The harm of a change of mind is no more than death.
translations.idiomatic: The harm of a change of mind is no more than death.

sentences.zh: 國本不立，萬一有如天象所告急兵之變，死且有罪，其為計亦已疏矣。

translations.literal: If the foundation of state is not established and by chance there is urgent military trouble as the heavens warned, death would still carry guilt; their planning is already loose.
translations.idiomatic: If the foundation of state is not established and by chance there comes the urgent military crisis the heavens foretold, death would still carry guilt—their planning is already too loose.

sentences.zh: 願以臣章示大臣，使其自擇死所。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty show my memorial to the grand ministers and let them choose their own place to die."
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty show my memorial to the grand ministers and let them choose their own place to die."

sentences.zh: 聞者股栗。

translations.literal: Those who heard shuddered.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard his words shuddered.

sentences.zh: 除兼侍御史知雜事，鎮以言不從，固辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief; Zhen because his words were not followed firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, but because his advice had not been heeded, he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 執政諭鎮曰：「今間言已入，為之甚難。」

translations.literal: The chief councilors instructed Zhen: "Rumors have already entered; it is very difficult now."
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilors told Zhen, "Rumors have already spread; it is very difficult now."

sentences.zh: 鎮復書執政曰：「事當論其是非，不當問其難易。

translations.literal: Zhen replied by letter: "Matters should be judged by right and wrong, not by difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied in a letter, "Matters should be judged by right and wrong, not by difficulty.

sentences.zh: 諸公謂今日難於前日，安知異日不難於今日乎？」

translations.literal: You gentlemen say today is harder than yesterday—how do you know tomorrow will not be harder than today?"
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen say today is harder than yesterday—how do you know tomorrow will not be harder than today?"

sentences.zh: 凡見上面陳者三，言益懇切，鎮泣，帝亦泣曰：「朕知卿忠，卿言是也，當更俟三二年。」

translations.literal: Three times in all he saw the emperor and spoke face to face, increasingly earnest; Zhen wept and the emperor also wept saying: "I know you are loyal; your words are right; we must wait another two or three years."
translations.idiomatic: Three times in all he saw the emperor and spoke face to face, growing ever more earnest; Zhen wept, and the emperor wept as well, saying, "I know you are loyal; your words are right; we must wait another two or three years."

sentences.zh: 章十九上，待命百餘日，鬚髮為白。

translations.literal: Nineteen memorials submitted; he waited over a hundred days until his beard and hair turned white.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted nineteen memorials and waited over a hundred days until his beard and hair turned white.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知不能奪，乃罷知諫院，改集賢殿修撰，糾察在京刑獄，同修起居注，遂知制誥。

translations.literal: The court knew they could not sway him; they removed him from the Remonstrance Bureau, made him Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Literature, Inspector of Capital Punishments, co-compiler of the Veritable Record, and then Drafting Officer for the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew they could not sway him; they removed him from the Remonstrance Bureau, made him Compiler at the Hall for Cherishing Literature, Inspector of Capital Punishments, co-compiler of the Veritable Record, and finally Drafting Officer for the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鎮雖解言職，無歲不申前議。

translations.literal: Though relieved of remonstrance duty, he appealed the former proposal every year without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Though relieved of his remonstrance duties, he appealed his former proposal every year without fail.

sentences.zh: 見帝春秋益高，每因事及之，冀以感動帝意。

translations.literal: Seeing the emperor's years advance, he seized every occasion to raise it, hoping to move the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's years advance, he seized every occasion to raise the matter, hoping to move the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 至是，因入謝，首言：「陛下許臣，今復三年矣，願早定大計。」

translations.literal: At this time, when entering to give thanks he first said: "Your Majesty promised me; three years have passed again; I wish an early settlement of the great plan."
translations.idiomatic: At this time, when he came to give thanks, he spoke first: "Your Majesty promised me; three years have passed again—I beg you settle the great plan soon."

sentences.zh: 又因祫享，獻賦以諷。

translations.literal: At a lineage-offering he also submitted a rhapsody as subtle admonition.
translations.idiomatic: At a lineage offering he also submitted a rhapsody as subtle admonition.

sentences.zh: 其後韓琦遂定策立英宗。

translations.literal: Thereafter Han Qi finally settled policy and established Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Han Qi finally settled the succession and established Emperor Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 中書議追尊濮王，兩制、臺諫與之異，詔禮官檢詳典禮。

translations.literal: The Secretariat deliberated posthumous honor for Prince Pu; the two drafting offices, the censorate and remonstrance bureau differed; an edict ordered ritual officers to examine canonical precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat deliberated posthumous honors for Prince Pu; the drafting offices, the censorate, and the remonstrance bureau disagreed; an edict ordered ritual officers to examine canonical precedent.

sentences.zh: 鎮判太常寺，率其屬言：「漢宣帝於昭帝為孫，光武於平帝為祖，其父容可稱皇考，議者猶非之，謂其以小宗合大宗之統也。

translations.literal: Zhen as president of the Directorate led his subordinates: "Han Xuandi was grandson to Emperor Zhao, Guangwu grandfather to Emperor Ping; their fathers might be styled Imperial Father-in-mourning, yet deliberators still faulted it as joining lesser lineage to greater lineage succession.
translations.idiomatic: As president of the Directorate of Sacrifices, Zhen led his subordinates in stating, "Han Xuandi was grandson to Emperor Zhao; Guangwu was grandfather to Emperor Ping. Their fathers might be styled Imperial Father, yet critics still faulted this as merging a lesser lineage into the succession of the greater lineage.

sentences.zh: 今陛下既以仁宗為考，又加於濮王，則其失非特漢二帝比。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has taken Emperor Renzong as father and also adds honors to Prince Pu; the error exceeds not only those two Han emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has taken Emperor Renzong as father and also adds honors to Prince Pu—the error exceeds even those of the two Han emperors.

sentences.zh: 凡稱帝若考，若寢廟，皆非是。」

translations.literal: All titles of emperor or father, shrine or temple, are wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Every title of emperor or father, every shrine or temple designation, is wrong."

sentences.zh: 執政怒，召鎮責曰：「方令檢詳，何遽列上！」

translations.literal: The chief councilors were angry and summoned Zhen to reproach him: "Examination was just ordered—why submit hastily!"
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilors were furious and summoned Zhen to rebuke him: "Examination was just ordered—why submit your findings so hastily!"

sentences.zh: 鎮曰：「有司得詔，不敢稽留，即以聞，乃其職也。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "When the office received the edict it dared not delay; to report immediately is its duty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "When the office received the edict it dared not delay; to report immediately is its duty.

sentences.zh: 奈何更以為罪乎？」

translations.literal: Why then treat it further as a crime?"
translations.idiomatic: Why then treat it as a crime on top of that?"

sentences.zh: 會草制，誤遷宰相官，改侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When drafting an edict he mistakenly promoted chief councilor ranks and was changed to Attendant Reader Academician.
translations.idiomatic: While drafting an edict he mistakenly promoted officials to chief councilor rank and was demoted to Attendant Reader Academician.

sentences.zh: 明年，還翰林，出知陳州。

translations.literal: The next year he returned to the Hanlin Academy and was sent out to govern Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned to the Hanlin Academy and was sent out to govern Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陳方飢，視事三日，擅發錢粟以貸。

translations.literal: Chen was then suffering famine; three days after taking office he unauthorizedly released treasury funds and grain to lend them out.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was then in famine. Only three days after taking office, he released treasury funds and grain on his own authority to lend to the people.

sentences.zh: 監司繩之急，即自劾，詔原之。

translations.literal: Supervisory officials pressed the case urgently; he immediately memorialized against himself, and an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory officials pressed the case harshly. He immediately submitted a self-indictment, and an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 是歲大熟，所貸悉還。

translations.literal: That year the harvest was abundant and all that had been lent was fully repaid.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought a plentiful harvest, and everything lent was fully repaid.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，復為翰林學士兼侍讀、知通進銀臺司。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne he was again made Hanlin Academician concurrently Attendant Reader and director of the Office for Transmission and the Silver Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong came to the throne, Zhen was again made Hanlin Academician and Attendant Reader, and director of the Office for Transmission and the Silver Terrace.

sentences.zh: 故事，門下封駁制旨，省審章奏，糾擿違滯，皆著所授敕，後乃刊去。

translations.literal: By precedent, when the Gate reviewed and rebutted imperial edicts, examined and audited memorials, and corrected delays and violations, all were recorded on the decree received; later this was excised from publication.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when the Gate reviewed and rebutted imperial edicts, examined memorials, and corrected delays and violations, all were recorded on the decree that had been received; later this practice was removed from published copies.

sentences.zh: 鎮始請復之，使知所守。

translations.literal: Zhen was first to request its restoration, so that officials would know what they were bound to uphold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was the first to request its restoration, so officials would know what they were bound to uphold.

sentences.zh: 王安石改常平為青苗，鎮言：「常平之法，起於漢盛時，視穀貴賤發斂，以便農末，最為近古，不可改。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi changed Ever-Normal Granaries to Green Sprouts; Zhen said: "The Ever-Normal method arose in Han's flourishing age, issuing and gathering according to grain's dearth and cheapness to benefit farmers and merchants—it is nearest antiquity and must not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi replaced the Ever-Normal Granary system with Green Sprouts loans. Zhen said, "The Ever-Normal method arose in the Han dynasty at its height, releasing and collecting grain according to whether prices were high or low to benefit farmers and merchants. It is the method closest to antiquity and must not be changed.

sentences.zh: 而青苗行於唐之衰世，不足法。

translations.literal: Green Sprouts was practiced in Tang's declining age and is not worth taking as model.
translations.idiomatic: Green Sprouts, by contrast, was practiced in the Tang dynasty's decline and is not worth emulating.

sentences.zh: 且陛下疾富民之多取而少取之，此正百步、五十步之間耳。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty hates that the wealthy take much and give little—this is precisely the difference between a hundred paces and fifty paces.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty resents that the wealthy take much and give little—this is precisely the difference between a hundred paces and fifty paces.

sentences.zh: 今有兩人坐市貿易，一人故下其直以相傾，則人皆知惡之，可以朝廷而行市道之所惡乎？」

translations.literal: Now suppose two men sit trading in the market; one deliberately lowers his price to crush the other, and all know it is hateful—can the court practice what the market hates?"
translations.idiomatic: Suppose two men trade in the market and one deliberately undercuts the other's price to drive him out—everyone knows that is despicable. Can the court practice what the marketplace itself condemns?"

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿在邇英言：「今預買紬絹，亦青苗之比。」

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing at the Imperial Study said: "Today's advance purchase of silk and satin is also comparable to Green Sprouts."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing said at the Imperial Study, "Today's advance purchase of silk and satin is comparable to Green Sprouts."

sentences.zh: 鎮曰：「預買，亦敝法也。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Advance purchase is also a worn-out method.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "Advance purchase is also a worn-out method.

sentences.zh: 若府庫有餘，當並去之，豈應援以為比。」

translations.literal: If the treasuries have surplus, both should be abolished together—how can one cite it for comparison?"
translations.idiomatic: If the treasuries have a surplus, both should be abolished together—how can one cite a bad method as a precedent?"

sentences.zh: 韓琦極論新法之害，送條例司疏駁，李常乞罷青苗錢，詔命分析，鎮皆封還。

translations.literal: Han Qi argued strongly against harms of the new laws and sent rebuttals from the Regulations Office; Li Chang begged to abolish Green Sprout money; edicts ordered analysis—Zhen sealed all back.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi argued forcefully against the harms of the new laws and sent rebuttals from the Regulations Office; Li Chang petitioned to abolish Green Sprout loans; edicts ordered analysis—and Zhen sealed every one back unopened.

sentences.zh: 詔五下，鎮執如初。

translations.literal: Edicts came down five times; Zhen held to his original stance.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts came down five times, and Zhen held firm to his original position.

sentences.zh: 司馬光辭樞密副使，詔許之，鎮再封還。

translations.literal: Sima Guang resigned as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs; the edict permitted it—Zhen sealed it back twice.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang resigned as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs; the edict approved his resignation—and Zhen sealed it back twice.

sentences.zh: 帝以詔直付光，不由門下。

translations.literal: The emperor gave the straight edict to Guang, not through the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor delivered the edict directly to Guang, bypassing the Gate.

sentences.zh: 鎮奏曰：「由臣不才，使陛下廢法，有司失職，乞解銀臺司。」

translations.literal: Zhen memorialized: "Through my incompetence Your Majesty abandoned law and officials lost duty; I beg to resign the Silver Terrace Office."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen memorialized, "Through my incompetence Your Majesty has abandoned the law and the responsible offices have failed in their duties. I beg to resign from the Silver Terrace Office."

sentences.zh: 舉蘇軾諫官，御史謝景溫奏罷之；

translations.literal: He recommended Su Shi for remonstrance office; Censor Xie Jingwen memorialized to remove him;
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Su Shi for the Remonstrance Bureau, but Censor Xie Jingwen memorialized to block the appointment;

sentences.zh: 舉孔文仲制科，文仲對策，論新法不便，罷歸故官。

translations.literal: He recommended Kong Wenzhong for the policy examination; Wenzhong in his answers discussed harms of the new laws and was dismissed to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Kong Wenzhong for the policy examination; Wenzhong in his answers criticized the new laws as harmful and was sent back to his former post.

sentences.zh: 鎮皆力爭之，不報。

translations.literal: Zhen struggled for both vigorously; no response.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen fought vigorously for both men, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 即上疏曰：「臣言不行，無顏復立於朝，請謝事。

translations.literal: He immediately memorialized: "My words are not carried out; I have no face to stand again at court; I beg to resign.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a memorial: "My words go unheeded; I have no face to remain at court. I beg to resign my post.

sentences.zh: 臣言青苗不見聽，一宜去；

translations.literal: My words on Green Sprouts were not heard—first reason to leave;
translations.idiomatic: My counsel on Green Sprouts went unheeded—that is the first reason I should leave;

sentences.zh: 薦蘇軾、孔文仲不見用，二宜去。

translations.literal: Recommending Su Shi and Kong Wenzhong were not used—second reason to leave.
translations.idiomatic: My recommendations of Su Shi and Kong Wenzhong were rejected—that is the second reason I should leave.

sentences.zh: 李定避持服，遂不認母，壞人倫，逆天理，而欲以為御史，御史臺為之罷陳薦，舍人院為之罷宋敏求、呂大臨、蘇頌，諫院為之罷胡宗愈。

translations.literal: Li Ding avoided mourning observance, would not acknowledge his mother, destroyed human relations and opposed heavenly principle, yet they wished to make him censor; the Censorate for this stopped recommending Chen; the Drafting Office stopped Song Minqiu, Lü Dalin, and Su Song; the Remonstrance Bureau stopped Hu Zongyu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ding avoided mourning observance and refused to acknowledge his mother, violating human relations and defying heavenly principle—yet they wished to appoint him censor. The Censorate halted its recommendations over this; the Drafting Office removed Song Minqiu, Lü Dalin, and Su Song; the Remonstrance Bureau removed Hu Zongyu.

sentences.zh: 王韶上書肆意欺罔，以興造邊事，事敗，則置而不問，反為之罪帥臣李師中；

translations.literal: Wang Shao memorialized recklessly deceiving to promote border affairs; when affairs failed they set it aside without inquiry and instead blamed Commander Li Shizhong;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao memorialized with reckless deception to stir up border conflicts; when his schemes failed they ignored the matter and instead blamed the frontier commander Li Shizhong;

sentences.zh: 及御史一言蘇軾，則下七路掎摭其過；

translations.literal: yet at one censor's word on Su Shi they sent down search through seven circuits for his faults;
translations.idiomatic: yet at a single censor's word against Su Shi, they dispatched investigators through seven circuits to hunt for his faults;

sentences.zh: 孔文仲則遣之歸任。

translations.literal: Kong Wenzhong they sent back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wenzhong they simply sent back to his former post.

sentences.zh: 以此二人況彼二人，事理孰是孰非，孰得孰失，其能逃聖鑒乎？

translations.literal: Comparing these two men with those two, which principle is right or wrong, which gain or loss—can it escape the sage's mirror?
translations.idiomatic: Compare these two cases with those two—which is right and which is wrong, which gains and which loses? Can such inconsistency escape Your Majesty's discerning eye?

sentences.zh: 言青苗有見效者，不過歲得什百萬緡錢，緡錢什百萬，非出於天，非出於地，非出於建議者之家，蓋一出於民耳。

translations.literal: Those who say Green Sprouts show results speak only of millions in strings yearly; those millions do not come from heaven, earth, or the reformers' homes—they come entirely from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Those who claim Green Sprouts are effective speak only of millions in strings of cash each year—but those millions do not fall from heaven, rise from earth, or come from the reformers' own households. They come entirely from the people.

sentences.zh: 民猶魚也，財猶水也，養民而盡其財，譬猶養魚而竭其水也。」

translations.literal: The people are like fish and wealth like water; nourishing people while exhausting their wealth is like nourishing fish while draining their water."
translations.idiomatic: The people are like fish and wealth is like water. To nourish the people while exhausting their wealth is like keeping fish while draining the pond dry."

sentences.zh: 疏五上，其後指安石用喜怒為賞罰，曰：「陛下有納諫之資，大臣進拒諫之計；

translations.literal: Five memorials submitted; later he pointed out Anshi used pleasure and anger for rewards and punishments, saying: "Your Majesty has the capacity to accept remonstrance, but grand ministers advance plans to reject remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted five memorials; later he charged that Anshi used personal pleasure and anger as the basis for rewards and punishments, saying, "Your Majesty has the capacity to accept remonstrance, yet your grand ministers advance plans to block it;

sentences.zh: 陛下有愛民之性，大臣用殘民之術。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has nature to love the people, but grand ministers use methods to harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has a nature that loves the people, yet your grand ministers employ methods that harm them.

sentences.zh: 臣知言入觸大臣之怒，罪且不測。

translations.literal: I know entering speech offends grand ministers' anger and punishment is unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: I know that entering such words will provoke the grand ministers' wrath and that my punishment is unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 然臣職獻替而無一言，則負陛下矣。」

translations.literal: Yet my office is to advise and replace, and without one word I fail Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Yet my office is to advise and correct, and if I speak not one word I fail Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 疏入，安石大怒，持其疏至手顫，自草制極詆之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Anshi was greatly angered, held it until his hand trembled, and himself drafted an edict harshly reviling him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Anshi was furious; he held it until his hand trembled and personally drafted an edict harshly denouncing him.

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎致仕，凡所得恩典，悉不與。

translations.literal: He retired as Vice Minister of Revenue; all favors granted were withheld.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Vice Minister of Revenue, and every favor normally granted on retirement was withheld.

sentences.zh: 鎮表謝，略曰：「願陛下集群議為耳目，以除壅蔽之奸，任老成為腹心，以養和平之福。」

translations.literal: Zhen's thank-you memorial said briefly: "I wish Your Majesty gather collective deliberation as eyes and ears to remove obstructing treachery, employ the experienced as heart and belly to nurture peaceful blessings."
translations.idiomatic: In his letter of thanks Zhen wrote briefly, "I wish Your Majesty would gather collective counsel as your eyes and ears to remove obstructing treachery, and employ the experienced as your heart and core to nurture the blessings of peace."

sentences.zh: 天下聞而壯之。

translations.literal: All under Heaven heard and were heartened.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven heard of it and were heartened.

sentences.zh: 安石雖詆之深切，人更以為榮。

translations.literal: Though Anshi reviled him deeply, people esteemed it still more as honor.
translations.idiomatic: Though Anshi reviled him bitterly, people esteemed Zhen all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 既退，蘇軾往賀曰：「公雖退，而名益重矣！」

translations.literal: After retiring, Su Shi came to congratulate him: "Though you retired, your name grows heavier!"
translations.idiomatic: After his retirement, Su Shi came to congratulate him, saying, "Though you have retired, your reputation has only grown heavier!"

sentences.zh: 鎮愀然曰：「君子言聽計從，消患於未萌，使天下陰受其賜，無智名，無勇功；

translations.literal: Zhen said somberly: "The gentleman whose words are heard and plans followed eliminates trouble before it sprouts, letting the realm secretly receive benefit—no reputation for wisdom, no merit for courage;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said somberly, "The true gentleman is he whose counsel is heard and whose plans are followed, who eliminates trouble before it sprouts and lets the realm receive benefit in secret—with no reputation for wisdom and no credit for courage;

sentences.zh: 吾獨不得為此，使天下受其害而吾享其名，吾何心哉！」

translations.literal: I alone could not do this, letting the realm suffer harm while I enjoy the name—what heart is that!"
translations.idiomatic: I alone could not do this—letting the realm suffer harm while I enjoy the fame. What sort of heart is that!"

sentences.zh: 日與賓客賦詩飲酒，或勸使稱疾杜門，鎮曰：「死生禍福，天也，吾其如天何！」

translations.literal: Daily with guests he composed poetry and drank wine; some urged him to feign illness and shut his door; Zhen said: "Life, death, fortune, and disaster are Heaven's—what can I do against Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Each day he composed poetry and drank wine with his guests. Some urged him to feign illness and shut his doors. Zhen said, "Life, death, fortune, and disaster belong to Heaven—what can I do against Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 同天節乞隨班上壽，許之，遂為令。

translations.literal: On the Same Heaven Festival he begged to follow the class in offering birthday felicitations; it was permitted, and became regulation.
translations.idiomatic: On the Same Heaven Festival he petitioned to join his class in offering birthday felicitations to the emperor; permission was granted, and it became permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 軾得罪，下臺獄，索與鎮往來書文甚急，猶上書論救。

translations.literal: When Shi offended and was put in the prison bureau, they urgently sought his correspondence with Zhen; Zhen still memorialized to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi fell afoul of the law and was imprisoned, investigators urgently sought his correspondence with Zhen—yet Zhen still submitted a memorial pleading for his rescue.

sentences.zh: 久之，徙居許。

translations.literal: After long time he moved residence to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he moved his residence to Xu.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，韓維言：「鎮在仁宗時，首啟建儲之議，未嘗以語人，人亦莫為言者。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended, Han Wei said: "Zhen in Emperor Renzong's time first opened the proposal to establish an heir, never told others, and others did not speak for him either."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Han Wei said, "During Emperor Renzong's reign Zhen was the first to raise the question of establishing an heir. He never spoke of it to others, and no one else spoke on his behalf either."

sentences.zh: 具以十九疏上之。

translations.literal: He submitted all nineteen memorials in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted all nineteen memorials in full.

sentences.zh: 拜端明殿學士，起提舉中太一宮兼侍讀，且欲以為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity, raised to oversee the Central Grand Unity Palace with concurrent study-reader, and they also wished to make him Vice Director of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity, recalled to oversee the Central Grand Unity Palace with concurrent study-reader duties, and the court also wished to make him Vice Director of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 鎮雅不欲起，從孫祖禹亦勸止之，遂固辭，改提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: Zhen by nature did not wish to rise; his nephew's son Zuyu also urged stopping; he firmly declined and was changed to oversee the Palace of Cherished Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen by temperament did not wish to return to office; his grandnephew Zuyu also urged him to stay home. He firmly declined and was instead assigned to oversee the Palace of Cherished Blessings.

sentences.zh: 祖禹謁告歸省，詔賜以龍茶，存勞甚渥。

translations.literal: Zuyu took leave to visit family; edict bestowed Dragon Tea; stored favors were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuyu took leave to visit his family, an edict bestowed Dragon Tea upon him; the emperor's favors were exceedingly generous.

sentences.zh: 復告老，以銀青光祿大夫再致仕，累封蜀郡公。

translations.literal: He again reported old age and retired second time as Silver Glory Grandee of Splendid Happiness, cumulatively enfeoffed Duke of Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He again reported his advanced age and retired a second time as Silver Glory Grandee of Splendid Happiness, and was cumulatively enfeoffed as Duke of Shu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 鎮於樂尤注意，自謂得古法，獨主房庶以律生尺之說。

translations.literal: Zhen paid special attention to music, claiming he obtained ancient methods, alone maintaining Fang Shu's theory of generating the foot-measure from pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen paid special attention to music, claiming he had recovered the ancient methods, and alone upheld Fang Shu's theory of deriving the standard foot-measure from the pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 司馬光謂不然，往復論難，凡數萬言。

translations.literal: Sima Guang said otherwise; they argued back and forth in tens of thousands of words.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang disagreed, and they argued back and forth in exchanges totaling tens of thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 初，仁宗命李照改定大樂，下王朴樂三律。

translations.literal: Initially Emperor Renzong ordered Li Zhao to revise the great music, lowering Wang Pu's music three pitches.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Emperor Renzong ordered Li Zhao to revise the court music, lowering Wang Pu's scale by three pitches.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，又詔胡瑗等考正。

translations.literal: In Huangyou he again ordered Hu Yuan and others to examine and correct.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou era he again ordered Hu Yuan and others to examine and correct it.

sentences.zh: 神宗時詔鎮與劉几定之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shenzong's time he ordered Zhen and Liu Ji to fix it.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Shenzong's reign he ordered Zhen and Liu Ji to fix it.

sentences.zh: 鎮曰：「定樂當先正律。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Fixing music must first correct the pitch pipes."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "To fix the music one must first correct the pitch pipes."

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「然，雖有師曠之聰，不以六律不能正五音。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So—even though one has Shi Kuang's hearing, without the six pitches one cannot correct the five tones."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "True—even one with Shi Kuang's hearing cannot correct the five tones without the six pitch pipes."

sentences.zh: 鎮作律尺、龠合、升斗、豆區、鬴斛，欲圖上之，又乞訪求真黍，以定黃鐘。

translations.literal: Zhen made pitch-foot measure, pipes, pecks, bushels, and measures, wishing to present diagrams; he also begged to seek true millet to fix the yellow bell.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen constructed pitch pipes, foot-measures, vessels, pecks, bushels, and grain measures, intending to present diagrams to the throne, and also petitioned to seek true millet grain to establish the yellow bell pitch.

sentences.zh: 而劉几即用李照樂，加用四清聲而奏樂成。

translations.literal: But Liu Ji immediately used Li Zhao's music, adding four clear tones and the performance was completed.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Ji immediately adopted Li Zhao's music, added four clear tones, and the performance was completed.

sentences.zh: 詔罷局，賜齎有加。

translations.literal: An edict dissolved the bureau; gifts were generous.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dissolved the bureau, and generous gifts were bestowed.

sentences.zh: 鎮曰：「此劉几樂也，臣何與焉。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "This is Liu Ji's music—what has it to do with me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "This is Liu Ji's music—what does it have to do with me?"

sentences.zh: 至是，乃請太府銅為之，逾年而成，比李照樂下一律有奇。

translations.literal: Only then did he request Grand Storehouse copper to make them; after more than a year they were completed, one odd pitch lower than Li Zhao's music.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he request copper from the Grand Storehouse to cast them; after more than a year they were completed, one pitch lower than Li Zhao's scale with a fractional remainder.

sentences.zh: 帝及太皇太后御延和殿，召執政同閱視，賜詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: The emperor and Grand Empress Dowager attended at the Yanhe Hall, summoned chief councilors to view together, and bestowed an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Grand Empress Dowager attended at the Yanhe Hall, summoned the chief councilors to view the instruments together, and bestowed an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 下之太常，詔三省、侍從、臺閣之臣，皆往觀焉。

translations.literal: It was sent down to the Directorate; an edict ordered three ministries, attendants, and censorate officials all to go view.
translations.idiomatic: The instruments were sent to the Directorate of Sacrifices, and an edict ordered officials of the three ministries, attendants, and censorate all to come view them.

sentences.zh: 鎮時已屬疾，樂奏三日而薨，年八十一。

translations.literal: Zhen was then already seriously ill; music was performed three days and he died, age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was already gravely ill at the time; the music was performed for three days, and then he died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰「忠文」。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Golden Glory Grandee of Splendid Happiness; posthumous title "Loyal and Literary."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Golden Glory Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with the posthumous epithet "Loyal and Literary."

sentences.zh: 鎮平生與司馬光相得甚歡，議論如出一口，且約生則互為傳，死則作銘。

translations.literal: Zhen in life was very congenial with Sima Guang; their opinions were as if from one mouth, and they agreed while living to write each other's biography and when dead to compose epitaphs.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life Zhen was on the closest terms with Sima Guang; their opinions were as if spoken from a single mouth, and they agreed that while living they would write each other's biography and when dead compose each other's epitaph.

sentences.zh: 光生為鎮《傳》，服其勇決；

translations.literal: While living Guang wrote Zhen's Biography, admiring his courage and resolve;
translations.idiomatic: While Zhen still lived, Guang wrote his Biography, admiring his courage and resolve;

sentences.zh: 鎮復銘光墓云：「熙寧奸朋淫縱，險詖憸猾，賴神宗洞察於中。」

translations.literal: Zhen in turn epitaphed Guang's tomb: "In Xining treacherous factions were wanton and devious, crafty and sly—thanks to Shenzong's penetration within."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen in turn composed Guang's tomb inscription: "In the Xining era treacherous factions were wanton and devious, crafty and sly—yet thanks to Shenzong's penetration within."

sentences.zh: 其辭峭峻。

translations.literal: The wording was severe and stern.
translations.idiomatic: The wording was severe and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 光子康屬蘇軾書之，軾曰：「軾不辭書，懼非三家福。」

translations.literal: Guang's son Kang entrusted Su Shi to write it; Shi said: "I do not decline writing, but fear it is not fortune for three families."
translations.idiomatic: Guang's son Kang asked Su Shi to write it out; Shi said, "I do not decline to write, but I fear it may not bring fortune to all three families."

sentences.zh: 乃易他銘。

translations.literal: They changed to another epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: They substituted another epitaph instead.

sentences.zh: 鎮清白坦夷，遇人必以誠，恭儉慎默，口不言人過。

translations.literal: Zhen was pure, open, and level; meeting people he always used sincerity, respectful, frugal, cautious, and silent, never speaking others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was pure, open, and straightforward; in dealing with others he was always sincere, respectful, frugal, cautious, and reticent, and never spoke of others' faults.

sentences.zh: 臨大節，決大議，色和而語壯，常欲繼之以死，雖在萬乘前，無所屈。

translations.literal: Facing great principle and deciding great deliberations, his expression was mild and words strong; he often wished to follow with death; even before the Son of Heaven he would not bend.
translations.idiomatic: When facing great principles and deciding weighty matters, his expression was mild but his words forceful; he was often ready to follow his counsel with his life, and even before the Son of Heaven he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 篤於行義，奏補先族人而後子孫，鄉人有不克婚葬者，輒為主之。

translations.literal: Sincere in acting righteousness, in memorials he supplemented distant clan before sons and grandsons; when fellow villagers could not marry or bury, he always arranged it for them.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply devoted to righteous conduct, in his memorials he recommended distant clansmen before his own sons and grandsons; when fellow villagers could not afford marriage or burial, he always arranged it for them.

sentences.zh: 兄鎡，卒於隴城，無子，聞其有遺腹子在外，鎮時未仕，徒步求之兩蜀間，二年乃得之，曰：「吾兄異於人，體有四乳，則兒亦必然。」

translations.literal: Elder brother Zan died at Longcheng without sons; hearing there was a posthumous son outside, Zhen then not yet in office walked seeking him between the two Shu for two years before finding him, saying: "My brother differed from others—his body had four nipples, so the child must be likewise."
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zan died at Longcheng without heirs; hearing that a posthumous son existed somewhere outside, Zhen—then still without office—walked on foot searching between the two Shu regions for two years before finding him, saying, "My brother was unlike other men—his body had four nipples, so the child must be the same."

sentences.zh: 已而果然，名曰百常。

translations.literal: In time it was indeed so; the name was Baichang.
translations.idiomatic: In time it proved true; the boy was named Baichang.

sentences.zh: 少受學於鄉先生龐直溫，直溫子昉卒於京師，鎮娶其女為孫婦，養其妻子終身。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under village teacher Pang Zhiwen; Zhiwen's son Fang died in the capital—Zhen married his daughter to his grandson and supported wife and children lifelong.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under the village teacher Pang Zhiwen; when Zhiwen's son Fang died in the capital, Zhen married his daughter to his grandson and supported Fang's wife and children for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 其學本《六經》，口不道佛、老、申、韓之說。

translations.literal: His learning rooted in the Six Classics; his mouth did not speak Buddhist, Daoist, Legalist, or stratagem doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: His learning was rooted in the Six Classics, and he never spoke of Buddhist, Daoist, Legalist, or stratagem doctrines.

sentences.zh: 契丹、高麗皆傳誦其文。

translations.literal: Khitan and Goryeo all transmitted and recited his writings.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Khitan and Goryeo transmitted and recited his writings.

sentences.zh: 少時賦《長嘯卻胡騎》，晚使遼，人相目曰：「此長嘯公也。」

translations.literal: In youth he composed "Long Whistling Turns Back the Nomad Cavalry"; in old age when sent to Liao, people pointed and said: "This is the Long Whistling Lord."
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he composed "Long Whistling Turns Back the Nomad Cavalry"; when sent to Liao in his old age, people pointed at him and said, "This is the Long Whistling Lord."

sentences.zh: 兄子百祿亦使遼，遼人首問鎮安否。

translations.literal: His nephew Baolu also was sent to Liao; Liao people first asked whether Zhen was well.
translations.idiomatic: When his nephew Bailu was also sent to Liao, the Liao people first asked whether Zhen was well.

sentences.zh: 從子 百祿

translations.literal: Nephew Bailu
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Bailu

sentences.zh: 百祿，字子功，鎮兄鍇之子也。

translations.literal: Bailu, styled Zigong, was son of Zhen's elder brother Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Bailu, whose style was Zigong, was the son of Zhen's elder brother Kai.

sentences.zh: 第進士，又舉才識兼茂科。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and also passed the Examination of Talent and Policy Combined.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination and also passed the Examination of Outstanding Talent and Comprehensive Policy.

sentences.zh: 時治平水災，大臣方議濮禮，百祿對策曰：「簡宗廟、廢祭祀，則水不潤下。

translations.literal: At the time there were floods in the Zhiping era and grand ministers debated Pu rites; Bailu in his answers said: "Simplify ancestral temples and abolish sacrifices, then water will not flow down harmoniously.
translations.idiomatic: At the time floods struck during the Zhiping era and grand ministers were debating the rites for Prince Pu; in his examination answers Bailu said, "Simplify the ancestral temples and abolish sacrifices, and water will not flow down in harmony.

sentences.zh: 昔漢哀尊共皇，河南、潁川大水；

translations.literal: Formerly Han Aidi honored the Co-Emperor, and Henan and Yingchuan had great floods;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when Emperor Ai of Han honored the Co-Emperor, Henan and Yingchuan suffered great floods;

sentences.zh: 孝安尊德皇，京師、郡國二十九大水。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiao'an honored Virtuous Emperor, and the capital and twenty-nine commanderies had great floods.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiao'an honored the Virtuous Emperor, the capital and twenty-nine commanderies suffered great floods.

sentences.zh: 蓋大宗隆，小宗殺；

translations.literal: For the greater lineage is elevated, the lesser lineage is reduced;
translations.idiomatic: For the greater lineage is elevated and the lesser lineage is diminished;

sentences.zh: 宗廟重，私祀輕。

translations.literal: ancestral temples are weighty, private sacrifices are light.
translations.idiomatic: the ancestral temples are weighty and private sacrifices are light.

sentences.zh: 今宜殺而隆，宜輕而重，是悖先王之禮。

translations.literal: Now what should be reduced is elevated, what should be light is made heavy—this violates the Former Kings' ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Now what should be diminished is elevated, and what should be light is made heavy—this violates the ritual of the Former Kings.

sentences.zh: 禮一悖，則人心失而天意睽，變異所由起也。」

translations.literal: Once ritual is violated, people's hearts are lost and Heaven's intent is estranged—strange transformations arise from this."
translations.idiomatic: Once ritual is violated, the people's hearts are lost and Heaven's intent is estranged—strange transformations arise from this."

sentences.zh: 對入三等。

translations.literal: His answer was placed third class.
translations.idiomatic: His answer was ranked in the third class.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，鄧綰舉為御史，辭不就。

translations.literal: In Xining, Deng Zong recommended him as censor; he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era Deng Zong recommended him as censor, but he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 提點江東、利、梓路刑獄，加直集賢院。

translations.literal: He supervised judicial affairs on Jiangdong, Li, and Zi circuits, and was added Direct Gentleman of the Collected Treasures.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial intendant for the Jiangdong, Li, and Zi circuits and was appointed Direct Gentleman of the Collected Treasures.

sentences.zh: 利州武守周永懿以賄敗，百祿請復至道故事，用文吏領兵，以轄邊界，從之。

translations.literal: Military prefect Zhou Yongyi of Li prefecture was ruined by bribery; Bailu asked to restore the Zhidao precedent of using civil officials to command troops to control the border—this was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The military prefect Zhou Yongyi of Li prefecture was ruined by bribery; Bailu petitioned to restore the Zhidao-era precedent of placing civil officials in command of troops to control the border, and the proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 熊本治瀘蠻事，有夷酋力屈請降，裨將賈昌言欲殺以為功，百祿諭之不聽，往謂本曰：「殺降不祥，活千人者封子孫。

translations.literal: Xiong Ben governed Lu barbarian affairs; a tribal chief submitted when strength failed; subordinate general Jia Changyan wished to kill him for merit; Bailu admonished him but he would not listen, went to tell Ben: "Killing those who surrender is inauspicious; saving a thousand lives enfeoffs descendants.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiong Ben was governing affairs with the Lu barbarians, a tribal chief whose strength had failed submitted in surrender; the subordinate general Jia Changyan wished to kill him for merit. Bailu admonished him but he would not listen, and went to tell Ben, "Killing those who surrender is inauspicious—he who saves a thousand lives will have his descendants enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 奈何容驕將橫境內乎？」

translations.literal: How can you tolerate arrogant generals crossing within the borders?"
translations.idiomatic: How can you tolerate arrogant generals running rampant within the borders?"

sentences.zh: 本矍然，即檄止之。

translations.literal: Ben started awake and immediately dispatched orders to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Ben started in alarm and immediately issued orders to stop it.

sentences.zh: 七年，召知諫院。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned to head the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was summoned to head the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 屬歲旱，請講求急務，收還法令之未便者，以救將死之民。

translations.literal: When drought struck that year, he asked to discuss urgent affairs and recall inconvenient laws to save people near death.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck that year, he petitioned to address urgent affairs and repeal inconvenient laws in order to save people on the brink of starvation.

sentences.zh: 論手實法曰：「造薄手實，許令告匿。

translations.literal: Discussing the hand-record law he said: "Making thin hand-records and permitting denunciation of concealment.
translations.idiomatic: On the hand-record law he said, "Issuing simplified household registers and permitting informants to denounce concealed property.

sentences.zh: 戶令雖有手實之文，而未嘗行。

translations.literal: The household ordinance though has hand-record text, yet it was never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The household ordinance contained provisions for hand-records, but they had never been enforced.

sentences.zh: 蓋謂使人自占，必不以實告，而明許告訐，人將為仇。

translations.literal: For it means having people report themselves—they surely will not report truthfully, while openly permitting denunciation, people will become enemies.
translations.idiomatic: For if people are made to report their own holdings, they will surely not report truthfully; yet if denunciation is openly permitted, people will become one another's enemies.

sentences.zh: 然則禮、義、廉、恥之風衰矣。」

translations.literal: Then the wind of ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame will decline."
translations.idiomatic: Then the spirit of ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame will wither away."

sentences.zh: 五路置三十七將，專督所部兵，至許辟置布衣參軍謀。

translations.literal: Thirty-seven generals were placed on five circuits to supervise their troops exclusively, even permitting recruitment of commoner military advisers.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-seven generals were appointed across five circuits to supervise their troops exclusively, and they were even permitted to recruit commoners as military advisers.

sentences.zh: 百祿察其中，或以恩澤市，或以瘝敗收，或未歷邊方，或起於群盜，疏列其亡狀者十四人，請仍舊制，將佐顓教閱，餘付之州縣，事多施行。

translations.literal: Bailu examined them: some traded on favor, some were recruited through bribery, some had never served on the frontier, some rose from bandit gangs; he listed fourteen unfit men and asked to restore the old system of generals and deputies exclusively drilling troops, the rest entrusted to prefectures and counties—many measures were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Bailu investigated them and found that some had bought their posts through favor, some through bribery, some had never served on the frontier, and some had risen from bandit gangs. He listed fourteen unfit men and asked to restore the old system whereby generals and deputies alone conducted troop drills, leaving the rest to prefectures and counties—and many of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 與徐禧治李士寧獄，奏士寧熒惑童婦，致不軌生心，罪死不赦。

translations.literal: With Xu Xi he tried the case of Li Shining, memorializing that Shining deluded children and women, causing rebellious intent, a crime death without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Xu Xi he tried the case of Li Shining, memorializing that Shining had deluded children and women and incited rebellious intent—a capital offense that merited no pardon.

sentences.zh: 禧右士寧，以為無罪。

translations.literal: Xi sided with Shining, deeming him innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Xi sided with Shining and declared him innocent.

sentences.zh: 執政主禧，貶百祿監宿州酒。

translations.literal: The chief councilors supported Xi and demoted Bailu to supervise wine tax at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilors sided with Xi and demoted Bailu to supervisor of the Suzhou wine monopoly.

sentences.zh: 元豐末，入為司門、吏部郎中、起居郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanfeng he entered as Gate Officer, Ministry of Personnel director, and Attendant on the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanfeng era he entered court service as Gate Officer, director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Attendant on the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended he was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 司馬光復差役法，患吏受賕，欲加流配。

translations.literal: Sima Guang restored the corvée labor law, worried officials took bribes, and wished to add exile punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang restored the corvée labor system, concerned that officials were taking bribes, and wished to add exile as punishment.

sentences.zh: 百祿固爭曰：「民今日執事，受謝於人，明日罷役，則以財賂人。

translations.literal: Bailu firmly argued: "Today the people perform duties and receive thanks from others; tomorrow when service ends they use wealth to bribe people.
translations.idiomatic: Bailu argued forcefully, "Today a commoner performs official duties and accepts payment from others; tomorrow when his term ends, he uses his wealth to bribe others.

sentences.zh: 苟繩以重典，黥面赭衣必將充塞道路。」

translations.literal: If bound by heavy statutes, tattooed faces and ochre robes will surely fill the roads."
translations.idiomatic: If punished under harsh statutes, tattooed faces and ochre prisoner's robes will surely fill the roads."

sentences.zh: 光悟曰：「微君言，吾不悉也。」

translations.literal: Guang understood and said: "Without your words I would not have known."
translations.idiomatic: Guang understood and said, "Without your words I would not have understood this."

sentences.zh: 遂已。

translations.literal: It was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou he became Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanyou he was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 諸郡以故鬥殺情可矜者請讞，法官曰：「宜貸。」

translations.literal: Various prefectures requested review for brawl-killings with pitiable circumstances; judges said: "Should commute."
translations.idiomatic: Various prefectures requested judicial review for brawl-killings with mitigating circumstances; the judges said, "Commutation is appropriate."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「殺人不死，法廢矣。」

translations.literal: Guang said: "If killers do not die, the law is abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "If killers do not die, the law is rendered void."

sentences.zh: 百祿曰：「謂之殺人，則可；

translations.literal: Bailu said: "To call it killing a person is acceptable;
translations.idiomatic: Bailu said, "To call it killing is acceptable;

sentences.zh: 若制刑以為無足疑，原情以為無足憫，則不可。

translations.literal: but if fixing punishment as without sufficient doubt and excusing feeling as without sufficient pity, that cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: but if the law treats the case as beyond doubt and the circumstances as beyond pity, that cannot be right.

sentences.zh: 今概之死，則二殺之科，自是遂無足疑憫者矣。」

translations.literal: Now executing all to death, then the two categories of killing from this point have no cases with sufficient doubt or pity."
translations.idiomatic: If all are executed to death, then the two categories of killing will from this point forward have no cases worthy of doubt or pity."

sentences.zh: 時又詔天下獄不當讞而輒讞者抵罪。

translations.literal: At the time there was also an edict that throughout the realm prisons not due for review yet reviewed would incur punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was also an edict that officials who submitted cases for review when review was not warranted would be punished.

sentences.zh: 有司重於請，至枉情以求合法。

translations.literal: Officials placed weight on petitions, even distorting circumstances to seek legal conformity.
translations.idiomatic: Officials placed such weight on petitions that they even distorted the facts to make cases conform to the law.

sentences.zh: 百祿曰：「熙寧之法，非可疑可憫而讞者免駁勘，元豐則刊之，近則有奏劾之詔，故官吏畏避，不憚論殺。」

translations.literal: Bailu said: "Under Xining law, those reviewed without doubt or pity were exempted from re-examination; Yuanfeng published this; recently there is the edict on impeachment, so officials fear and avoid, not hesitating to argue for execution."
