translations.idiomatic: Bailu said, "Under the Xining law, cases reviewed without grounds of doubt or pity were exempted from re-examination; the Yuanfeng code published this rule; and recently there has been an edict on impeachment—so officials are fearful and no longer hesitate to argue for execution."

sentences.zh: 因條五年死貸之數以聞。

translations.literal: He then listed five years' numbers of death commutations and reported.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted statistics on death sentences commuted over the past five years.

sentences.zh: 門下省猶駁正當貸者，又例在有司者還中書，百祿又爭之，後悉從其請。

translations.literal: The Gate still rejected those who should be commuted; there was also precedent returning cases in officials' hands to the Secretariat; Bailu argued again, and later all followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate still rejected cases that should have been commuted; there was also a precedent returning cases in officials' hands to the Secretariat. Bailu argued again, and in the end all his requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 改吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 議者欲汰胥吏，呂大防趣廢其半，百祿曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Deliberators wished to eliminate clerks; Lü Dafang urged abolishing half; Bailu said: "Cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed eliminating clerks; Lü Dafang urged abolishing half of them. Bailu said, "That cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 廢半則失職者眾，不若以漸消之，自今闕吏勿補，不數歲，減斯過半矣。」

translations.literal: Abolishing half then those losing office are many; better to diminish gradually—from now when posts are vacant do not fill them; within a few years reduction will exceed half."
translations.idiomatic: Abolishing half at once would leave too many without employment; it is better to reduce them gradually—from now on, when posts fall vacant, do not fill them, and within a few years the number will be reduced by more than half."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: They did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 都水王孝先議回河故道，大防意向之，命百祿行視。

translations.literal: Director of Waterways Wang Xiaoxian proposed returning the Yellow River to its old course; Dafang inclined toward it and ordered Bailu to inspect on site.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaoxian, Director of Waterways, proposed diverting the Yellow River back to its old course; Dafang was inclined to agree and ordered Bailu to inspect the site.

sentences.zh: 百祿以東流高仰，而河勢順下，不可回，即馳奏所以然之狀，且取神宗詔令勿塞故道者並上之。

translations.literal: Bailu held that the eastern flow was high and elevated while the river's momentum ran downward—it could not be turned back; he immediately rushed a memorial on the reasons and submitted together Shenzong's edict not to block the old course.
translations.idiomatic: Bailu argued that the eastern channel ran high while the river's momentum flowed downward, so it could not be diverted back. He immediately submitted an urgent memorial explaining why, and attached Shenzong's edict forbidding blockage of the old course.

sentences.zh: 大防猶謂：「大河東流，中國之險限。

translations.literal: Dafang still said: "The great river flowing east is China's strategic barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang still argued, "The great river flowing eastward is China's strategic barrier.

sentences.zh: 今塘濼既壞，界河淤淺，河且北注矣。」

translations.literal: Now the pond marshes are ruined and the border river silted shallow—the river will soon pour north."
translations.idiomatic: Now the pond marshes are ruined and the border river silted shallow—the river will soon shift northward."

sentences.zh: 百祿言：「塘濼有限寇之名，無禦寇之實。

translations.literal: Bailu said: "The pond marshes have the name of limiting enemies but not the reality of repelling enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Bailu replied, "The pond marshes have the name of limiting enemies but not the reality of repelling them.

sentences.zh: 借使河徙而北，敵始有下流之憂，乃吾之利也。

translations.literal: Suppose the river shifts north—the enemy would then have worry over the lower reach; that would be our advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the river shifted north, the enemy would then face the threat of a downstream attack—that would be to our advantage.

sentences.zh: 先帝明詔具在，奈何妄動搖之。」

translations.literal: The former emperor's clear edicts are all in place—how can we rashly shake them?"
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor's clear edicts are still in force—how can we rashly overturn them?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: It was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The project was then halted.

sentences.zh: 俄兼侍讀，進翰林學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrent study-reader and advanced to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed concurrent study-reader and promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 為帝言分別邪正之目，凡導人主以某事者為公正，某事者為奸邪，以類相反，凡二十餘條。

translations.literal: He told the emperor categories for distinguishing wicked from upright: whatever guides the ruler by certain acts is upright, certain acts wicked—opposite by category, over twenty items in all.
translations.idiomatic: He explained to the emperor categories for distinguishing the wicked from the upright: whatever guides the ruler toward certain conduct is upright, and whatever guides him toward other conduct is wicked—twenty-odd paired opposites in all.

sentences.zh: 願概斯事以觀其情，則邪正分矣。

translations.literal: I wish to survey these matters to observe their disposition, then wicked and upright will be divided.
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty to survey these matters and observe people's true dispositions—then the wicked and the upright will be clearly separated.

sentences.zh: 以龍圖閣學士知開封府。

translations.literal: As Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall he governed Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall he was appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 勤於民事，獄無繫囚。

translations.literal: Diligent in civilian affairs, the prisons had no detained prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: He was diligent in civil affairs, and the prisons held no detained prisoners.

sentences.zh: 僚吏欲以圄空聞，百祿曰：「千里之畿，無一人之獄，此至尊之仁，非尹功也。」

translations.literal: Staff wished to report empty prisons; Bailu said: "A thousand-li capital district with not one person in prison—this is the supreme one's benevolence, not the prefect's merit."
translations.idiomatic: His staff wished to report that the prisons were empty. Bailu said, "In a capital district a thousand li across, with not a single prisoner in the jails—this reflects the supreme ruler's benevolence, not the prefect's merit."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: He did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 經數月，復為翰林學士，拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: After several months he again became Hanlin Academician and was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was again made Hanlin Academician and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是歲郊祀，議合祭天地，禮官以「昊天有成命」為言。

translations.literal: That year at suburban sacrifice they debated combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth; ritual officers cited "Vast Heaven Has Fixed the Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: That year at the suburban sacrifice, officials debated combining the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth; ritual officers cited the ode "Vast Heaven Has Fixed the Mandate."

sentences.zh: 百祿曰：「此三代之禮，奈何復欲合祭乎？

translations.literal: Bailu said: "This is the ritual of the Three Dynasties—why again wish combined sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: Bailu said, "This is the ritual of the Three Dynasties—why do you wish to combine the sacrifices again?

sentences.zh: 『成命』之頌，祀天祭地，均歌此詩，亦如春夏祈穀而歌《噫嘻》，亦豈為一祭哉？」

translations.literal: The hymn "Fixed Mandate" is sung both for sacrificing to Heaven and sacrificing to Earth—just as spring and summer pray for grain and sing "Yi Xi"—how could it be for one sacrifice alone?"
translations.idiomatic: The hymn "Fixed Mandate" is sung at sacrifices to both Heaven and Earth—just as "Yi Xi" is sung at spring and summer grain prayers—how could it prove they are a single sacrifice?"

sentences.zh: 爭久不決，質於帝前。

translations.literal: Debate long unresolved, they submitted the question before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The debate dragged on without resolution, and the question was submitted before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 宰相曰：「百祿之言，禮經也；

translations.literal: The chief councilor said: "Bailu's words are ritual canon;
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor said, "Bailu's words follow the ritual canon;

sentences.zh: 今日之用，權制也。

translations.literal: today's use is expedient regulation.
translations.idiomatic: today's practice is an expedient measure.

sentences.zh: 陛下始郊見，宜以並事天地為恭。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's first suburban appearance should take serving Heaven and Earth together as reverence."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's first suburban appearance should take serving Heaven and Earth together as an act of reverence."

sentences.zh: 於是合祭。

translations.literal: Thereupon combined sacrifice was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The combined sacrifice was then performed.

sentences.zh: 熙河范育言：「阿里骨酷暴且病，溫溪心八族皆思內附，可以計納。」

translations.literal: Fan Yu of Xihe said: "Aligu is cruel and violent and ill; the eight clans of Wenxi and Xin all wish to submit inward—can be won by stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yu of Xihe said, "Aligu is cruel, violent, and ill; the eight clans of Wenxi and Xin all wish to submit to the court—we can win them by stratagem."

sentences.zh: 百祿曰：「中國以信撫四夷，阿里骨未有過，溪心虛實未可知，無釁而動，非策也。」

translations.literal: Bailu said: "China uses trust to soothe the four barbarians; Aligu has no fault yet; Wenxi and Xin's truth is unknown; moving without provocation is not strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Bailu replied, "China wins over the four barbarians through trust and kindness. Aligu has committed no offense, and whether Wenxi and Xin's intentions are genuine is unknown. To act without provocation is no strategy."

sentences.zh: 又請進築納迷等三城，百祿曰：「是皆良田，為必爭之地，我既城之，若賊騎時出，我何以耕？

translations.literal: They also asked to advance building three cities including Nami; Bailu said: "These are all fertile fields and ground sure to be contested; once we fortify them, if enemy cavalry sallies forth when will we plow?
translations.idiomatic: They also asked to advance construction of three cities including Nami. Bailu said, "These are all fertile fields and ground certain to be contested. Once we fortify them, if enemy cavalry sallies forth at will, how can we farm?

sentences.zh: 後雖欲棄之，為費已甚，亦不能矣。」

translations.literal: Later even if we wish to abandon them, the expense is already great and it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Later, even if we wished to abandon them, the expense would already be too great to do so."

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of his advice.

sentences.zh: 右僕射蘇頌坐稽留除書免，百祿以同省罷為資政殿學士、知河中，徙河陽、河南。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Su Song was dismissed for delaying appointment patents; Bailu was removed from the same ministry as Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Hezhong, transferred to Heyang and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Su Song was dismissed for delaying appointment documents; Bailu, removed from the same ministry, was made Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Hezhong, then transferred to Heyang and Henan.

sentences.zh: 薨，年六十五，贈銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died, age sixty-five, posthumously granted Silver Glory Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-five and was posthumously granted the title Silver Glory Grandee of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子祖述，監潁州酒稅，攝獄掾，閱具獄，活兩死囚，州人以為神。

translations.literal: His son Zushu supervised Yingzhou wine tax, acted as prison clerk, reviewed completed cases, saved two death-row prisoners—the prefecture considered it miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zushu supervised the Yingzhou wine tax, served as acting prison clerk, reviewed completed cases, and saved two prisoners condemned to death—the prefecture regarded it as miraculous.

sentences.zh: 知鞏縣，鑿南山導水入洛，縣無水患，文彥博稱其能。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Gong county he tunneled the southern mountain to channel water into the Luo—the county had no flood disaster; Wen Yanbo praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Gong County he tunneled through the southern mountains to channel water into the Luo River, and the county suffered no more floods; Wen Yanbo praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 以父墮黨籍，監中嶽廟。

translations.literal: Because his father fell into faction registers he supervised the Central Peak temple.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had been struck from the faction registers, he was assigned to supervise the Central Peak temple.

sentences.zh: 久之，通判涇州。

translations.literal: After long time he was deputy prefect of Jing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed deputy prefect of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知台州，奏罷黃甘、葛蕈之貢。

translations.literal: As prefect of Taizhou he memorialized to abolish tribute of yellow citrus and kudzu mushroom.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Taizhou he memorialized to abolish the tribute of yellow citrus and kudzu mushrooms.

sentences.zh: 主管西京御史臺。

translations.literal: He oversaw the Western Capital Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed in charge of the Western Capital Censorate.

sentences.zh: 靖康多難，避地至汝州。

translations.literal: In the many troubles of Jingkang he fled to Ru prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil of the Jingkang era he fled to Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 汝守趙子櫟邀與共守，於是旁郡盡陷，汝獨全。

translations.literal: Ru prefect Zhao Zilie invited him to defend together; thus neighboring prefectures all fell while Ru alone was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Ru, Zhao Zilie, invited him to defend the city together; neighboring prefectures all fell, but Ru alone was preserved.

sentences.zh: 累官朝議大夫，卒。

translations.literal: Cumulatively reaching Court Deliberation Grandee, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose cumulatively to Court Deliberation Grandee and died.

sentences.zh: 從弟祖禹。

translations.literal: Younger cousin Zuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Younger cousin: Zuyu.

sentences.zh: 從孫 祖禹

translations.literal: Grandnephew: Zuyu
translations.idiomatic: Grandnephew: Zuyu

sentences.zh: 祖禹，字淳甫，一字夢得。

translations.literal: Zuyu, styled Chunfu, with another style Mengde.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu, whose style was Chunfu and who also used the style Mengde.

sentences.zh: 其生也，母夢一偉丈夫被金甲入寢室，曰：「吾漢將軍鄧禹。」

translations.literal: At his birth his mother dreamed a great man in golden armor entered the bedchamber saying: "I am Han general Deng Yu."
translations.idiomatic: At his birth his mother dreamed that a great man clad in golden armor entered the bedchamber and said, "I am the Han general Deng Yu."

sentences.zh: 既寤，猶見之，遂以為名。

translations.literal: When she awoke she still saw him and thus took it as his name.
translations.idiomatic: When she awoke she still saw him, and thus gave the child his name.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，叔祖鎮撫育如己子。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his uncle-grandfather Zhen raised and nurtured him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, his granduncle Zhen raised and nurtured him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 祖禹自以既孤，每歲時親賓慶集，慘怛若無所容，閉門讀書，未嘗預人事。

translations.literal: Zuyu because he was orphaned, whenever kin and guests gathered for seasonal celebrations was grief-stricken as if with no place to be, shut his door reading books, never participating in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was orphaned, whenever kin and guests gathered for seasonal celebrations Zuyu was grief-stricken and ill at ease; he shut his door to read and never participated in social affairs.

sentences.zh: 既至京師，所與交游，皆一時聞人。

translations.literal: Once he reached the capital, those with whom he associated were all renowned men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the capital, all those with whom he associated were renowned men of the age.

sentences.zh: 鎮器之曰：「此兒，天下士也。」

translations.literal: Zhen treasured him saying: "This boy is a man of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen treasured him and said, "This boy is a man of the realm."

sentences.zh: 進士甲科。

translations.literal: He passed jinshi in the top class.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the top class.

sentences.zh: 從司馬光編修《資治通鑒》，在洛十五年，不事進取。

translations.literal: He followed Sima Guang compiling the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, at Luoyang fifteen years, not pursuing advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted Sima Guang in compiling the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, spending fifteen years at Luoyang without seeking advancement.

sentences.zh: 書成，光薦為秘書省正字。

translations.literal: When the book was completed Guang recommended him as Corrector of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was completed, Guang recommended him as Corrector of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時王安石當國，尤愛重之。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Anshi held the state and especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Anshi held power and especially valued him.

sentences.zh: 王安國與祖禹友善，嘗諭安石意，竟不往謁。

translations.literal: Wang Anguo was friendly with Zuyu and once conveyed Anshi's intent, yet he never went to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anguo was on friendly terms with Zuyu and once conveyed Anshi's intentions, yet Zuyu never went to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 富弼致仕居洛，素嚴毅，杜門罕與人接，待祖禹獨厚；

translations.literal: Fu Bi retired and dwelt at Luoyang, by nature stern and resolute, shutting his door rarely receiving people, yet treated Zuyu alone generously;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi had retired to Luoyang; stern and resolute by nature, he kept his doors closed and rarely received visitors, yet he treated Zuyu with special generosity;

sentences.zh: 疾篤，召授以密疏，大抵論安石誤國及新法之害，言極憤切。

translations.literal: When gravely ill he summoned him and entrusted a secret memorial, broadly discussing Anshi's error to the state and harms of new laws, words extremely indignant.
translations.idiomatic: When gravely ill he summoned Zuyu and entrusted him with a secret memorial, broadly discussing how Anshi had misled the state and the harms of the new laws, in language of extreme indignation.

sentences.zh: 弼薨，人皆以為不可奏，祖禹卒上之。

translations.literal: When Bi died all thought it should not be submitted; Zuyu finally submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi died everyone thought the memorial should not be submitted; Zuyu finally submitted it anyway.

sentences.zh: 神宗崩，祖禹上疏論喪服之制曰：「先王制禮，君服同於父，皆斬衰三年，蓋恐為人臣者不以父事其君。

translations.literal: When Shenzong died Zuyu memorialized on mourning-garment regulations: "Former kings made ritual: the ruler's mourning same as for father, all top-grade three-year mourning, fearing lest subjects not treat their ruler as father.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong died, Zuyu submitted a memorial on mourning regulations: "The Former Kings established ritual so that mourning for the ruler was the same as for a father—top-grade three-year mourning for both—fearing lest subjects fail to treat their ruler as they would a father.

sentences.zh: 自漢以來，不惟人臣無服，人君遂不為三年之喪。

translations.literal: From Han onward not only did subjects have no mourning garments, but rulers also ceased three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han dynasty onward, not only did subjects cease wearing mourning garments, but rulers also ceased observing three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 國朝自祖宗以來，外廷雖用易月之制，宮中實行三年服。

translations.literal: Our dynasty from the ancestors onward, though the outer court used the month-replacement system, within the palace three-year garments were actually practiced.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty, from the founding ancestors onward, the outer court used the abbreviated month-replacement mourning, but within the palace three-year mourning was actually observed.

sentences.zh: 君服如古典，而臣下猶依漢制，故十二日而小祥，朞而又小祥，二十四日而大祥，再朞而又大祥。

translations.literal: The ruler's garments followed ancient canon while subjects still followed Han system, thus twelve days then lesser felicity, one cycle then again lesser felicity, twenty-four days then greater felicity, two cycles then again greater felicity.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's mourning followed the ancient canon while subjects still followed Han practice, so there was lesser felicity at twelve days, lesser felicity again at one cycle, greater felicity at twenty-four days, and greater felicity again at two cycles.

sentences.zh: 既以日為之，又以月為之，此禮之無據者也。

translations.literal: Both counting by days and counting by months—this is ritual without basis.
translations.idiomatic: To count both by days and by months—this is ritual without proper basis.

sentences.zh: 古者再朞而大祥，中月而禫。

translations.literal: In antiquity greater felicity came at two cycles, and the chan sacrifice at mid-month.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity greater felicity came at two cycles, and the chan sacrifice at the middle of the month.

sentences.zh: 禫，祭之名，非服之色。

translations.literal: Chan is the name of a sacrifice, not the color of a garment.
translations.idiomatic: Chan is the name of a sacrifice, not the color of mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 今乃為之慘服三日然後禫，此禮之不經者也。

translations.literal: Now they make somber garments for three days then chan—this is ritual that violates canon.
translations.idiomatic: Now they wear somber garments for three days and then perform the chan sacrifice—this is ritual that violates canonical practice.

sentences.zh: 服既除，至葬又服之，祔廟後即吉，才八月而遽純吉，無所不佩，此又禮之無漸者也。

translations.literal: Garments already removed, at burial they don them again; after enshrining in the ancestral temple they immediately use auspicious garments—only eight months then suddenly pure auspicious, wearing everything—this again is ritual without gradual transition.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning garments are removed, then donned again at burial; after enshrinement in the ancestral temple they immediately switch to auspicious dress—only eight months pass before they are suddenly in full auspicious attire, wearing every ornament—this again is ritual without gradual transition.

sentences.zh: 朔望，群臣朝服以造殯宮，是以吉服臨喪；

translations.literal: On new and full moon all officials in court dress visit the mourning palace—thus using auspicious dress to attend mourning;
translations.idiomatic: On the new and full moon, all officials in court dress visit the mourning palace—thus attending a funeral in auspicious dress;

sentences.zh: 人主衰服在上，是以先帝之服為人主之私喪，此二者皆禮之所不安也。」

translations.literal: the ruler's mourning garments above, thus making the former emperor's mourning the ruler's private mourning—these two are both what ritual cannot rest easy with."
translations.idiomatic: while the ruler wears mourning garments above—thus treating the former emperor's mourning as the ruler's private family mourning—both of these are what ritual cannot accommodate."

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，擢右正言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, [he] was promoted to Right Rectifying Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong took the throne, Zuyu was promoted to Right Rectifying Censor.

sentences.zh: 呂公著執政，祖禹以婿嫌辭，改祠部員外郎，又辭。

translations.literal: Lü Gongzhu held power; Zuyu, citing the taboo of being his son-in-law, declined, was changed to Foreign Gentleman of the Temple Ministry, and declined again.
translations.idiomatic: With Lü Gongzhu directing the government, Zuyu withdrew citing the impropriety of serving under his father-in-law; he was reassigned as Foreign Gentleman of the Temple Ministry but declined that post as well.

sentences.zh: 除著作佐郎、修《神宗實錄》檢討，遷著作郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Compiler and examiner for compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong, then moved up to Compiler with concurrent palace lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Compiler and examiner for the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong, then promoted to Compiler with concurrent duty as palace lecturer.

sentences.zh: 神宗既祥，祖禹上疏宣仁后曰：「今即吉方始，服御一新，奢儉之端，皆由此起。

translations.literal: After Shenzong's second mourning period ended, Zuyu memorialized Empress Dowager Xuanren: "Now the end of mourning has just begun, dress and regalia are all renewed — the beginnings of extravagance and frugality all arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period for Emperor Shenzong had ended, Zuyu submitted a memorial to Empress Dowager Xuanren saying, "The mourning period has only just concluded and court dress and furnishings are already being renewed; the choice between extravagance and austerity begins here.

sentences.zh: 凡可以盪心悅目者，不宜有加於舊。

translations.literal: Whatever can sway the heart and please the eye should not be increased beyond what was before.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing that delights the senses should exceed what was used in the past.

sentences.zh: 皇帝聖性未定，睹儉則儉，睹奢則奢，所以訓導成德者，動宜有法。

translations.literal: The emperor's sagely nature is not yet fixed: seeing thrift he is thrifty, seeing extravagance he is extravagant; whatever trains and guides the formation of virtue, in every movement there should be method.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's character is not yet formed: he will imitate thrift when he sees thrift and extravagance when he sees extravagance. Every act that shapes his moral cultivation should follow a fixed standard.

sentences.zh: 今聞奉宸庫取珠，戶部用金，其數至多，恐增加無已，願止於未然。

translations.literal: Now I hear the Inner Treasury is taking pearls and the Ministry of Revenue is using gold, the quantities very great; I fear increase without end and wish it stopped before it happens.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that the Inner Treasury is drawing pearls and the Ministry of Revenue is spending gold in great quantities. I fear these expenses will grow without limit and ask that they be halted before the habit takes hold.

sentences.zh: 崇儉敦樸，輔養聖性，使目不視靡曼之色，耳不聽淫哇之聲，非禮勿言，非禮勿動，則學問日益，聖德日隆，此宗社無疆之福。」

translations.literal: Uphold thrift and foster plainness, assist in nurturing the sagely nature, so the eyes do not behold seductive colors, the ears do not hear licentious sounds, what is not ritual do not speak, what is not ritual do not do — then learning daily grows and sagely virtue daily rises; this is boundless fortune for altar and state."
translations.idiomatic: Honor austerity and simplicity in nurturing the emperor's character: let his eyes not see alluring sights, his ears not hear decadent music; let him speak and act only as ritual permits. Then his learning will deepen day by day and his virtue will ascend — the boundless blessing of dynasty and state."

sentences.zh: 故事，服除當開樂置宴，祖禹以為因除服而開樂設宴，則似除服而慶賀，非君子不得已而除之之意，不可。

translations.literal: By precedent, when mourning dress is removed music should be opened and a banquet set; Zuyu held that to open music and set a banquet because mourning dress is removed seems like celebrating the removal of mourning, not the intent of the gentleman who removes it only when unavoidable — it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent called for music and a feast when mourning ended. Zuyu argued that holding celebrations upon leaving mourning would make it look like a congratulation rather than the sober completion the rites intend, and urged that it not be done.

sentences.zh: 夏暑權罷講，祖禹言：「陛下今日之學與不學，繫他日治亂。

translations.literal: In summer heat lectures were temporarily suspended; Zuyu said: "Your Majesty's studying or not studying today is tied to order and disorder on another day.
translations.idiomatic: During the summer heat lectures were temporarily suspended. Zuyu said, "Whether Your Majesty studies today will determine whether the realm knows order or chaos tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 如好學，則天下君子欣慕，願立於朝，以直道事陛下，輔佐德業，而致太平；

translations.literal: If he loves learning, then gentlemen throughout the realm admire and rejoice, wishing to stand at court, to serve Your Majesty by the straight Way, assist virtue and achievement, and bring great peace;
translations.idiomatic: If he loves learning, gentlemen throughout the realm will admire him and gladly take office, serving Your Majesty with integrity, aiding his moral cultivation, and bringing the realm to peace;

sentences.zh: 不學，則小人皆動其心，務為邪諂，以竊富貴。

translations.literal: If he does not study, then petty men all stir their hearts, striving for wicked flattery to steal wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: If he does not study, petty men will set their minds on him, striving through flattery and deceit to seize wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 且凡人之進學，莫不於少時，今聖質日長，數年之後，恐不得如今日之專，竊為陛下惜也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, for all people advancing in learning there is none not in youth; now the sagely substance daily grows, and after several years I fear one cannot have today's concentration — I privately regret this for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, everyone advances in learning chiefly in youth. As Your Majesty's talents mature day by day, in a few years he may no longer enjoy the undivided attention of today. I grieve this on Your Majesty's behalf."

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎，又召試中書舍人，皆不拜。

translations.literal: He was moved to Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Chambers, then summoned to examination for Secretariat Drafter — he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Chambers and then summoned to qualify as Secretariat Drafter, but declined both appointments.

sentences.zh: 呂公著薨，召拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Lü Gongzhu died, [Zuyu] was summoned and appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Gongzhu died, Zuyu was summoned and appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 首上疏論人主正心修身之要，乞太皇太后日以天下之勤勞、萬民之疾苦、群臣之邪正、政事之得失，開導上心，曉然存之於中，使異日眾說不能惑，小人不能進。

translations.literal: First he memorialized on the essentials of the ruler rectifying the mind and cultivating the person, begging the Grand Empress Dowager daily to use the realm's toils, the myriad people's suffering, ministers' wickedness and uprightness, and affairs' gains and losses to open and guide the imperial heart, clearly storing them within, so that on another day many opinions cannot confuse and petty men cannot advance.
translations.idiomatic: He first memorialized on how a ruler should rectify his mind and cultivate his person, asking the Grand Empress Dowager daily to instruct the emperor with the realm's labors, the people's suffering, the integrity or corruption of ministers, and the successes and failures of policy, keeping these truths clear in his heart so that later no clamor of opinion could mislead him and no petty man could gain access.

sentences.zh: 蔡確既得罪，祖禹言：「自乾興以來，不竄逐大臣六十餘年，一旦行之，流傳四方，無不震聳。

translations.literal: After Cai Que had been punished, Zuyu said: "Since Qianxing there have been more than sixty years without banishing great ministers; to do it in one stroke, spreading to the four quarters, none do not startle and tremble.
translations.idiomatic: After Cai Que had been punished, Zuyu said, "For more than sixty years since the Qianxing era no great minister had been banished. To do so suddenly will send shock through every corner of the realm.

sentences.zh: 確去相已久，朝廷多非其黨，間有偏見異論者，若一切以為黨確去之，懼刑罰失中，而人情不安也。」

translations.literal: Que left the chancellorship long ago; the court mostly are not his faction; occasionally there are biased views and differing opinions — if one treats all alike as Que's faction being removed, I fear punishments lose their balance and human feelings are unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: Que left the chancellorship long ago, and most at court are not his partisans. A few hold biased or dissenting views. If every such case is treated as banishment of Que's clique, I fear punishments will lose their proper measure and public sentiment will grow uneasy."

sentences.zh: 蔡京鎮蜀，祖禹言：「京小有才，非端良之士。

translations.literal: Cai Jing was stationed over Shu; Zuyu said: "Jing has minor talent but is not an upright and good man.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing was posted to govern Shu, Zuyu said, "Jing has a little talent but is not a upright and trustworthy man.

sentences.zh: 如使守成都，其還，當使執政，不宜崇長。」

translations.literal: If he is made to guard Chengdu, on his return he will be made to hold power — he should not be exalted and nurtured."
translations.idiomatic: If he is sent to govern Chengdu, on his return he will surely be elevated to high office. He should not be encouraged and promoted."

sentences.zh: 時大臣欲於新舊法中有所創立。

translations.literal: At that time great ministers wished to create something new between the new and old laws.
translations.idiomatic: At that time leading ministers wished to devise innovations somewhere between the new and old laws.

sentences.zh: 祖禹以為：「朝廷既察王安石之法為非，但當復祖宗之舊，若出於新舊之間，兩用而兼存之，紀綱壞矣。」

translations.literal: Zuyu held: "The court has already perceived Wang Anshi's laws as wrong; one should only restore the ancestors' old ways. If one goes between new and old, using both and keeping both, the statutes and guidelines are ruined."
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu argued, "The court has already recognized Wang Anshi's laws as mistaken and should simply restore the institutions of the ancestors. To stand between new and old, employing and preserving both, would wreck the fundamental order of government."

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was moved to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 吳中大水，詔出米百萬斛、緡錢二十萬振救。

translations.literal: Great flood in Wu; edict issued a million hu of grain and two hundred thousand strings of cash for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu suffered severe flooding, an edict released a million hu of grain and two hundred thousand strings of cash for relief.

sentences.zh: 諫官謂訴災者為妄，乞加驗考。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials said those reporting disaster were false and begged added verification and investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials claimed the disaster reports were exaggerated and asked that the reports be investigated and verified.

sentences.zh: 祖禹封還其章，云：「國家根本，仰給東南。

translations.literal: Zuyu sealed and returned their memorial, saying: "The state's foundation depends for supply on the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu sealed and returned their memorial, writing, "The foundation of the state depends on supplies from the southeast.

sentences.zh: 今一方赤子，呼天赴訴，開口仰哺，以脫朝夕之急。

translations.literal: Now in one region infants in swaddling clothes cry to Heaven and rush to plead, opening mouths to look up for feeding, to escape the urgency of morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Now the common people of that region cry out to Heaven in their distress, mouths open waiting to be fed, desperate to escape their immediate peril.

sentences.zh: 奏災雖小過實，正當略而不問。

translations.literal: Reporting disaster though slightly exceeding fact, one should rightly overlook and not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Even if disaster reports slightly exaggerate the facts, that is precisely when they should be overlooked rather than prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 若稍施懲譴，恐後無復敢言者矣。」

translations.literal: If one slightly applies punishment and reprimand, I fear afterward none will again dare speak."
translations.idiomatic: If even mild punishment is imposed, I fear no one will dare speak out again."

sentences.zh: 兼國史院修撰，為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Concurrently State History Academy compiler, made Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as compiler at the State History Academy and was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 論擇監司守令曰：「祖宗分天下為十八路，置轉運使、提點刑獄，收鄉長、鎮將之權悉歸於縣，收縣之權歸於州，州之權歸於監司，監司之權歸於朝廷。

translations.literal: Discussing selection of circuit commissioners and prefectural and county magistrates he said: "The ancestors divided the realm into eighteen circuits, established transport commissioners and judicial intendants, gathered village heads' and garrison commanders' powers all back to the county, gathered county powers back to the prefecture, prefectural powers back to the circuit commissioner, circuit commissioners' powers back to the court.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial on selecting circuit commissioners, prefects, and magistrates he wrote, "The ancestors divided the realm into eighteen circuits and appointed transport commissioners and judicial intendants, concentrating the powers of village heads and garrison commanders in the counties, county powers in the prefectures, prefectural powers in the circuit commissioners, and circuit commissioners' powers in the central court.

sentences.zh: 上下相維，輕重相制，建置之道，最為合宜。

translations.literal: Above and below mutually sustain, light and heavy mutually restrain — the way of establishment is most fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Superior and subordinate mutually sustain one another, weight and counterweight mutually check each other — this institutional design is the most fitting.

sentences.zh: 監司付以一路，守臣付以一州，令宰付以一縣，皆與天子分土而治，其可不擇乎？

translations.literal: Circuit commissioners are entrusted with one circuit, prefectural officials with one prefecture, magistrates with one county — all share land with the Son of Heaven in governing; how can they not be selected?
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commissioners govern entire circuits, prefects entire prefectures, and magistrates entire counties — each shares in ruling the realm with the emperor. How can their appointment be anything but deliberate?

sentences.zh: 祖宗嘗有考課之法，專察諸路監司，置簿於中書，以稽其要。

translations.literal: The ancestors once had examination-and-rating laws, specially inspecting circuit commissioners of all circuits, setting registers at the Secretariat to check essentials.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestors once maintained performance-review regulations focused on circuit commissioners, keeping registers at the Secretariat to track their essential duties.

sentences.zh: 今宜委吏部尚書，取當為州者，條別功狀以上三省，三省召而察之，苟其人可任，則以次表用之。

translations.literal: Now one should entrust the Minister of Personnel, take those fit to be prefects, itemize merits and submit upward to the Three Departments; the Three Departments summon and inspect them — if the person can be entrusted, then in order present and use him.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Personnel should now identify candidates for prefectural office, list their achievements, and submit the lists to the Three Departments. The departments should summon and examine them, and if a man is fit for duty, recommend him for appointment in proper order.

sentences.zh: 至官，則令監司考其課績，終歲之後，可以校優劣而施黜陟焉。

translations.literal: On reaching office, then order circuit commissioners to examine their course achievements; after the year's end, one can compare excellence and inferiority and apply demotion and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, circuit commissioners should evaluate their performance, and at year's end their merits can be compared and promotions or dismissals applied accordingly.

sentences.zh: 如此則得人必多，監司、郡守得人，縣令不才，非所患也。」

translations.literal: Thus obtaining able men will certainly be many; if circuit commissioners and commandery prefects obtain able men, county magistrates without talent are not what is feared."
translations.idiomatic: In this way many able men will be found. If circuit commissioners and prefects are well chosen, incompetent county magistrates need not be a serious concern."

sentences.zh: 聞禁中覓乳媼，祖禹以帝年十四，非近女色之時，上疏勸進德愛身，又乞宣仁后保護上躬，言甚切至。

translations.literal: Hearing the inner palace was seeking wet-nurses, Zuyu, because the emperor was fourteen and it was not the time to approach feminine beauty, memorialized urging advance in virtue and care for the person, also begging Empress Dowager Xuanren to protect the emperor's person — words very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that the inner palace was seeking wet-nurses, Zuyu — noting that the emperor was only fourteen and not yet at an age to be near women — memorialized urging moral self-cultivation and care for his health, and also asked Empress Dowager Xuanren to guard the emperor's person. His language was exceedingly earnest.

sentences.zh: 既而宣仁諭祖禹，以外議皆虛傳，祖禹覆上疏曰：「臣言皇帝進德愛身，宜常以為戒。

translations.literal: Then Xuanren instructed Zuyu that outside talk was all empty rumor; Zuyu again memorialized: "Your servant's words that the emperor should advance virtue and care for his person should constantly be taken as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren then told Zuyu that the outside rumors were all false. Zuyu submitted another memorial: "What I said about the emperor advancing in virtue and guarding his health should remain a constant warning.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后保護上躬，亦願因而勿忘。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager protecting the emperor's person — I also wish thereby not to forget.
translations.idiomatic: I also hope Your Majesty will not forget the Grand Empress Dowager's duty to protect the emperor's person.

sentences.zh: 今外議雖虛，亦足為先事之戒。

translations.literal: Now outside talk though empty is also sufficient to serve as warning before the event.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the outside rumors are false, they are still sufficient warning before trouble arises.

sentences.zh: 臣侍經左右，有聞於道路，實懷私憂，是以不敢避妄言之罪。

translations.literal: Your servant attends the classics at the emperor's side; there are things heard on the road; I truly harbor private worry — therefore I dare not avoid the crime of reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: As one who attends the emperor in his studies, I hear things on the streets and bear private anxiety; therefore I dare not shrink from the charge of speaking rashly.

sentences.zh: 凡事言於未然，則誠為過；

translations.literal: For all matters, speaking before they happen is truly fault;
translations.idiomatic: To speak of any matter before it has happened may indeed seem presumptuous;

sentences.zh: 及其已然，則又無所及，言之何益？

translations.literal: when it has already happened, then again there is nothing to reach — of what use is speaking?
translations.idiomatic: but once it has already happened, nothing can be done — of what use would speech be then?

sentences.zh: 陛下寧受未然之言，勿使臣等有無及之悔。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty would rather receive words before the event than make your servants have regret that nothing could be done."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty would do better to hear warnings before events occur than leave your servants with the regret of words that came too late."

sentences.zh: 拜翰林學士，以叔百祿在中書，改侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Academician; because his uncle Bailu was in the Secretariat, he was changed to Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin Academician, but because his uncle Bailu served in the Secretariat he was reassigned as Academician Expositor.

sentences.zh: 百祿去，復為之。

translations.literal: When Bailu left, [Zuyu] was again made [Hanlin Academician].
translations.idiomatic: When Bailu left office, Zuyu was again appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 范氏自鎮至祖禹，比三世居禁林，士論榮慕。

translations.literal: The Fan clan from Zhen to Zuyu, three generations in succession dwelling in the Forbidden Grove, gentlemen's discussion honored and admired.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhen to Zuyu, three generations of the Fan family in succession held posts in the Hanlin Academy, a source of honor and envy among scholars.

sentences.zh: 宣仁太后崩，中外議論洶洶，人懷顧望，在位者畏懼，莫敢發言。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanren died, inside and outside discussion surged and roared; people harbored looking-back hesitation; those in office were afraid — none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Xuanren died, debate within and beyond the court grew turbulent. People hesitated and looked about; those in office were afraid, and none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 祖禹慮小人乘間害政，乃奏曰：「陛下方攬庶政，延見群臣，此國家隆替之本，社稷安危之機，生民休戚之端，君子小人進退消長之際，天命人心去就離合之時也，可不畏哉？

translations.literal: Zuyu feared petty men would seize the interval to harm government and memorialized: "Your Majesty is just gathering the many affairs and extending audience to the host of ministers — this is the root of the state's rise and fall, the pivot of altar and state's safety and peril, the beginning of the people's weal and woe, the juncture of gentlemen and petty men's advance, retreat, waning, and waxing, the time of Heaven's mandate and human hearts' going, staying, parting, and joining — can one not fear?
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that petty men would seize the moment to harm the government, Zuyu memorialized, "Your Majesty is just taking hold of affairs and receiving the ministers. This is the foundation of the state's rise or fall, the hinge of its safety or ruin, the source of the people's welfare or suffering, the moment when gentlemen and petty men advance or retreat, and the hour when Heaven's mandate and popular sentiment unite or divide. How can one not tremble before it?

sentences.zh: 先后有大功於宗社，有大德於生靈，九年之間，始終如一。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager had great merit for altar and state and great virtue for living creatures; within nine years, from beginning to end it was one.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager rendered great service to dynasty and state and great kindness to the people; for nine years her conduct was unwavering.

sentences.zh: 然群小怨恨，亦為不少，必將以改先帝之政、逐先帝之臣為言，以事離間，不可不察也。

translations.literal: Yet the host of petty men's resentment was also not small; they will certainly use changing the late emperor's policies and expelling the late emperor's ministers as their words, using affairs to sow division — this must be examined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the resentment of petty men was considerable. They will surely speak of overturning the late emperor's policies and driving out his ministers, using such matters to sow division. This must not escape scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 先后因天下人心，變而更化。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager, following the realm's human hearts, changed and further transformed.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager, responding to the will of the realm, changed course and brought reform.

sentences.zh: 既改其法，則作法之人有罪當退，亦順眾言而逐之。

translations.literal: Since the laws were already changed, those who made the laws had guilt and should withdraw — also following the multitude's words in expelling them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the laws were changed, those who devised them were guilty and ought to withdraw; their removal also followed the voice of the people.

sentences.zh: 是皆上負先帝，下負萬民，天下之所仇疾而欲去之者也，豈有憎惡於其間哉？

translations.literal: These all above failed the late emperor, below failed the myriad people — what the realm hated and wished to remove; how could there be hatred between them?
translations.idiomatic: They had failed the late emperor above and the people below; the realm hated them and wished them gone. How could there be personal animosity in the matter?

sentences.zh: 惟辨析是非，深拒邪說，有以奸言惑聽者，付之典刑，痛懲一人，以警群慝，則貼然無事矣。

translations.literal: Only distinguish right and wrong, deeply reject wicked doctrines; whoever uses treacherous words to confuse the hearing — hand to statutory punishment, sternly punish one man to warn the host of wickedness, then all is calm and without affair.
translations.idiomatic: Only distinguish truth from falsehood and firmly reject perverse doctrines. Whoever uses deceitful words to mislead Your Majesty should be handed to the law; punish one man severely to warn the wicked host, and all will be tranquil.

sentences.zh: 此等既誤先帝，又欲誤陛下，天下之事，豈堪小人再破壞邪？」

translations.literal: These sorts already misled the late emperor and again wish to mislead Your Majesty — affairs of the realm, how can they bear petty men destroying again?"
translations.idiomatic: These men already misled the late emperor and now wish to mislead Your Majesty. Can the affairs of the realm endure another ruin at the hands of petty men?"

sentences.zh: 初，蘇軾約俱上章論列，諫草已具，見祖禹疏，遂附名同奏，曰：「公之文，經世之文也。」

translations.literal: Earlier Su Shi had agreed to submit memorials together in discussion; the remonstrance draft was ready; seeing Zuyu's memorial, he then attached his name to the same submission, saying: "Your lordship's writing is writing that orders the age."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Su Shi had agreed to submit a joint memorial; his draft was already prepared. When he saw Zuyu's memorial he added his name to the same submission, saying, "Your writing is the kind that orders an age."

sentences.zh: 竟不復出其稿。

translations.literal: In the end he did not again produce his draft.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not submit his own draft.

sentences.zh: 祖禹又言：「陛下承六世之遺烈，當思天下者祖宗之天下，人民者祖宗之人民，百官者祖宗之百官，府庫者祖宗之府庫。

translations.literal: Zuyu again said: "Your Majesty inherits six generations' transmitted glory; one should think the realm is the ancestors' realm, the people the ancestors' people, the hundred officials the ancestors' hundred officials, the treasuries the ancestors' treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu also wrote, "Your Majesty inherits the accumulated glory of six reigns. He should remember that the realm is the realm of the ancestors, the people are the people of the ancestors, the officials are the officials of the ancestors, and the treasuries are the treasuries of the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 一言一動，如臨之在上，質之在傍，則可以長享天下之奉。

translations.literal: Every word and movement, as if they were above looking down, as if they were at the side examining — then one can long enjoy the realm's offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Let every word and deed be as if the ancestors looked down from above and stood witness at his side; then he may long enjoy the realm's devotion.

sentences.zh: 先后以大公至正為心，罷安石、惠卿所造新法，而行祖宗舊政。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager took great impartiality and utmost rectitude as her heart, abolished the new laws Anshi and Huiqing made, and practiced the ancestors' old government.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager took supreme impartiality as her guide, abolished the new laws devised by Anshi and Huiqing, and restored the policies of the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 故社稷危而復安，人心離而復合，乃至遼主亦戒其臣勿生事曰：『南朝專行仁宗之政矣。』

translations.literal: Thus altar and state were perilous and again secure, human hearts parted and again joined — even to the Liao ruler admonishing his ministers not to stir trouble, saying: "The Southern Court exclusively practices Emperor Renzong's government."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the state, once imperiled, was made secure again and popular hearts reunited. Even the Liao ruler warned his ministers not to provoke trouble, saying, "The Southern Court is now devoted solely to the policies of Emperor Renzong."

sentences.zh: 外夷之情如此，中國之人心可知。

translations.literal: The outer barbarians' sentiment is thus — the Central Realm's human hearts can be known.
translations.idiomatic: If foreign peoples felt thus, the hearts of the Chinese can readily be imagined.

sentences.zh: 先后日夜苦心勞力，為陛下立太平之基。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager day and night bitter in heart and laboring in strength, for Your Majesty established the foundation of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night the Empress Dowager labored with anguished devotion to lay the foundation of peace for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 願守之以靜，恭己以臨之，虛心以處之，則群臣邪正，萬事是非，皆瞭然於聖心矣。

translations.literal: I wish to guard it with quiet, respect the self in facing it, empty the heart in handling it — then ministers' wickedness and uprightness, ten thousand affairs' right and wrong, all are clear in the sagely heart.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty preserve it through tranquility, govern with humble self-restraint, and meet affairs with an open mind; then the integrity or corruption of ministers and the right and wrong of every matter will all stand clear before the imperial mind.

sentences.zh: 小人之情專為私，故不便於公；

translations.literal: Petty men's disposition is devoted to private interest, therefore inconvenient for the public;
translations.idiomatic: Petty men are devoted to private interest and therefore ill at ease with the public good;

sentences.zh: 專為邪，故不便於正；

translations.literal: devoted to wickedness, therefore inconvenient for uprightness;
translations.idiomatic: devoted to what is crooked and therefore ill at ease with what is upright;

sentences.zh: 專好動，故不便於靜。

translations.literal: devoted to loving movement, therefore inconvenient for quiet.
translations.idiomatic: devoted to agitation and therefore ill at ease with tranquility.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下痛心疾首，以為刻骨之戒。」

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty, heart pained and head aching, take this as a warning carved in bone."
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty take this to heart with deepest grief and keep it as a warning engraved in bone."

sentences.zh: 章累上，不報。

translations.literal: Memorials piled up in submission; no response.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorial after memorial, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 忽有旨召內臣十餘人，祖禹言：「陛下親政以來，四海傾耳，未聞訪一賢臣，而所召者乃先內侍，必謂陛下私於近習，望即賜追改。」

translations.literal: Suddenly there was an order summoning more than ten inner attendants; Zuyu said: "Since Your Majesty's personal rule, the four seas incline their ears; I have not heard of visiting one worthy minister, yet those summoned are first inner attendants — all will say Your Majesty is partial to near favorites; I hope you immediately bestow reversal and change."
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly an edict summoned more than ten inner attendants. Zuyu said, "Since Your Majesty began to rule in person the realm has listened eagerly, yet not one worthy minister has been sought while inner attendants are summoned first. All will conclude that Your Majesty favors his intimate servants. I beg that the order be immediately rescinded."

sentences.zh: 因請對，曰：「熙寧之初，王安石、呂惠卿造立新法，悉變祖宗之政，多引小人以誤國，勳舊之臣屏棄不用，忠正之士相繼遠引。

translations.literal: He therefore requested audience and said: "At the beginning of Xining, Wang Anshi and Lü Huiqing created and established new laws, wholly changing the ancestors' government, drawing in many petty men to mislead the state; meritorious old ministers were shut out and not used, loyal upright men in succession were driven far away.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested an audience and said, "At the start of the Xining era Wang Anshi and Lü Huiqing devised new laws and wholly overturned the policies of the ancestors, bringing in many petty men who misled the state. Meritorious veterans were cast aside, and upright men were driven from office one after another.

sentences.zh: 又用兵開邊，結怨外夷，天下愁苦，百姓流徙。

translations.literal: Again they used troops to open borders, bred resentment among outer barbarians; the realm was sorrowful and bitter, the hundred people drifted and migrated.
translations.idiomatic: They also waged war to expand the frontiers, earning the hatred of foreign peoples. The realm groaned in misery and the people were driven from their homes.

sentences.zh: 賴先帝覺悟，罷逐兩人，而所引群小，已佈滿中外，不可復去。

translations.literal: Relying on the late emperor's awakening, the two men were dismissed and expelled, but the host of petty men they drew in already spread throughout inside and outside — they cannot again be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to the late emperor's awakening the two men were dismissed, but the petty men they had brought in already filled every corner of the government and could no longer be uprooted.

sentences.zh: 蔡確連起大獄，王韶創取熙河，章惇開五溪，沈起擾交管，沈括、徐禧、俞充、种諤興造西事，兵民死傷皆不下二十萬。

translations.literal: Cai Que repeatedly raised great prosecutions; Wang Shao pioneered taking Xihe; Zhang Dun opened the Five Streams; Shen Qi disturbed Jiaozhi trade; Shen Kuo, Xu Xi, Yu Chong, and Chong E launched and created western affairs — soldiers and civilians dead and wounded were none less than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que launched successive great prosecutions; Wang Shao pioneered the seizure of the Xihe region; Zhang Dun opened the Five Streams; Shen Qi disrupted trade in Jiaozhi; Shen Kuo, Xu Xi, Yu Chong, and Chong E stirred up western campaigns — military and civilian dead and wounded numbered no fewer than two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 先帝臨朝悼悔，以謂朝廷不得不任其咎。

translations.literal: The late emperor facing court mourned and repented, holding that the court could not but bear the blame.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor, grieving at court, held that the government could not escape responsibility for these disasters.

sentences.zh: 以至吳居厚行鐵冶之法於京東，王子京行茶法於福建，蹇周輔行鹽法於江西，李稷、陸師閔行茶法、市易於西川，劉定教保甲於河北，民皆愁痛嗟怨，比屋思亂。

translations.literal: To the extent that Wu Juhou practiced iron-smelting laws in Jingdong, Wang Zijing practiced tea laws in Fujian, Jian Zhoufu practiced salt laws in Jiangxi, Li Ji and Lu Shimin practiced tea laws and market trade in Xichuan, Liu Ding taught baojia in Hebei — the people all were sorrowful, pained, sighing, and resentful; household by household they thought of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Juhou imposed iron-smelting laws in Jingdong; Wang Zijing imposed tea laws in Fujian; Jian Zhoufu imposed salt laws in Jiangxi; Li Ji and Lu Shimin imposed tea and market-trade laws in Xichuan; Liu Ding taught the baojia system in Hebei — everywhere the people groaned in pain and resentment, and household after household brooded on rebellion.

sentences.zh: 賴陛下與先后起而救之，天下之民，如解倒縣。

translations.literal: Relying on Your Majesty and the Empress Dowager rising to rescue them, the realm's people were like undoing an inverted suspension.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Your Majesty and the Empress Dowager rising to rescue them, the people of the realm were as if released from hanging upside down.

sentences.zh: 惟是向來所斥逐之人，窺伺事變，妄意陛下不以修改法度為是，如得至左右，必進奸言。

translations.literal: Only those formerly expelled and driven away watch for changes in affairs, wrongly thinking Your Majesty does not regard revising the laws and standards as right — if they reach your side, they will certainly advance treacherous words.
translations.idiomatic: Only those who were formerly expelled now watch for a turn of events, wrongly supposing that Your Majesty does not approve of changing the laws. If they reach your side they will surely offer wicked counsel.

sentences.zh: 萬一過聽而復用之，臣恐國家自此陵遲，不復振矣。」

translations.literal: If by any chance [Your Majesty] over-listens and again employs them, your servant fears the state from this will decline and not again revive."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty should by any mischance heed them and restore them to office, I fear the state will from that moment decline beyond recovery."

sentences.zh: 又論：「漢、唐之亡，皆由宦官。

translations.literal: He again argued: "Han and Tang's fall were all from eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: He argued further, "The fall of Han and Tang was in every case brought about by eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 自熙寧、元豐間，李憲、王中正、宋用臣輩用事總兵，權勢震灼。

translations.literal: From Xining and Yuanfeng between, Li Xian, Wang Zhongzheng, Song Yongchen and the like held affairs and commanded troops; power and influence blazed dazzling.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xining and Yuanfeng eras Li Xian, Wang Zhongzheng, Song Yongchen, and their like held power and commanded armies, their authority dazzling and overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 中正兼幹四路，口敕募兵，州郡不敢違，師徒凍餒，死亡最多；

translations.literal: Zhongzheng concurrently managed four circuits, by oral edict recruited troops — prefectures and commanderies dared not disobey; armies froze and starved, deaths were most numerous;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng simultaneously managed four circuits, recruiting troops by oral edict that no prefecture dared refuse; his armies froze and starved, and deaths were greatest among them;

sentences.zh: 憲陳再舉之策，致永樂摧陷；

translations.literal: Xian presented the plan to campaign again, causing Yongle's collapse and fall;
translations.idiomatic: Xian urged renewed campaigns, bringing about the disaster at Yongle;

sentences.zh: 用臣興土木之工，無時休息，罔市井之微利，為國斂怨。

translations.literal: Yongchen raised earth-and-wood works, without time for rest, netting the market streets' slight profits, for the state gathering resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchen launched construction projects without cease, seizing petty profits from the marketplace and heaping resentment upon the state.

sentences.zh: 此三人者，雖加誅戮，未足以謝百姓。

translations.literal: These three men, though execution were added, would not suffice to answer to the hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: Even execution would not have been enough to atone to the people for these three men.

sentences.zh: 憲雖已亡，而中正、用臣尚在，今召內臣十人，而憲、中正之子皆在其中。

translations.literal: Though Xian is already dead, Zhongzheng and Yongchen are still alive; now ten inner attendants are summoned, and Xian's and Zhongzheng's sons are all among them.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xian is dead, Zhongzheng and Yongchen still live. Now ten inner attendants are summoned, and among them are the sons of Xian and Zhongzheng.

sentences.zh: 二人既入，則中正、用臣必將復用，願陛下念之。」

translations.literal: Once the two men enter, then Zhongzheng and Yongchen will certainly again be employed — I wish Your Majesty to reflect on this."
translations.idiomatic: Once these two enter office, Zhongzheng and Yongchen will surely be restored to power. I beg Your Majesty to consider this."

sentences.zh: 時紹述之論已興，有相章惇意。

translations.literal: At that time the doctrine of continuing the legacy had already risen; there were those who wished to make Zhang Dun chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: By then the movement to restore the late emperor's policies had arisen, and some wished to make Zhang Dun chancellor.

sentences.zh: 祖禹力言惇不可用，不見從，遂請外。

translations.literal: Zuyu strenuously said Dun could not be used; he was not followed, and [Zuyu] then requested outer [post].
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu argued forcefully that Zhang Dun must not be employed, but was not heeded and therefore asked for an outside appointment.

sentences.zh: 上且欲大用，而內外梗之者甚眾，乃以龍圖閣學士知陝州。

translations.literal: The emperor moreover wished to greatly employ him, but inside and outside those who blocked were very many; he was then made Dragon Diagram Pavilion Academician and prefect of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still wished to employ him in high office, but opposition within and without the court was widespread, and he was instead appointed Dragon Diagram Pavilion Academician and prefect of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 言者論祖禹修《實錄》詆誣，又摭其諫禁中雇乳媼事，連貶武安軍節度副使、昭州別駕，安置永州、賀州，又徙賓、化而卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: Critics argued Zuyu in compiling the Veritable Records slandered and defamed, also gathered his remonstrance on hiring wet-nurses in the inner palace; he was in succession demoted Military Commissioner Vice Commissioner of Wu'an Army, Zhao Prefecture Administrator-on-Leave, settled at Yongzhou and Hezhou, again moved to Bin and Hua and died, age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged that in compiling the Veritable Records Zuyu had slandered the court, and they also seized on his memorial against hiring wet-nurses in the inner palace. He was successively demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of the Wu'an Army and Administrator-on-Leave of Zhao Prefecture, exiled to Yongzhou and Hezhou, then transferred to Bin and Hua, where he died at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 祖禹平居恂恂，口不言人過。

translations.literal: Zuyu in ordinary times was respectful and deferential, mouth not speaking others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life Zuyu was modest and deferential and never spoke of others' faults.

sentences.zh: 至遇事，則別白是非，不少借隱。

translations.literal: When it came to encountering affairs, then he distinguished right and wrong, not slightly borrowing concealment.
translations.idiomatic: But when affairs arose he distinguished right from wrong without the least concealment.

sentences.zh: 在邇英守經據正，獻納尤多。

translations.literal: In Er'ying he upheld the classics and held to rectitude; presentations and acceptances were especially many.
translations.idiomatic: In the Er'ying Hall he upheld the classics and held firm to principle, and his remonstrances were especially numerous.

sentences.zh: 嘗講《尚書》至「內作色荒，外作禽荒」六語，拱手再誦，卻立云：「願陛下留聽。」

translations.literal: Once lecturing on the Documents of History to the six phrases "within making color wasteland, without making bird wasteland," he joined hands and recited twice, stepped back and stood saying: "I wish Your Majesty to remain and listen."
translations.idiomatic: Once, lecturing on the Book of Documents, he came to the six words "Within, he makes dissipation his pursuit; without, he makes the chase his sport." He bowed with joined hands, recited them twice, stepped back, and said, "I beg Your Majesty to pause and heed these words."

sentences.zh: 帝首肯再三，乃退。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent again and again, then [Zuyu] withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded repeatedly in assent, and only then did Zuyu withdraw.

sentences.zh: 每當講前夕，必正衣冠，儼如在上側，命子弟侍，先按講其說。

translations.literal: Whenever on the eve of lecture he must straighten cap and robes, solemn as if above at his side, ordered sons and younger brothers to attend, first going through and lecturing his explanation.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of each lecture he would dress formally, as solemn as if standing beside the emperor, summon his sons and younger brothers to attend, and rehearse his exposition beforehand.

sentences.zh: 開列古義，參之時事，言簡而當，無一長語，義理明白，粲然成文。

translations.literal: He opened and arrayed ancient meanings, compared them to current affairs — words brief yet fitting, not one long phrase; principles clear, brilliantly forming writing.
translations.idiomatic: He set forth the meanings of the ancients and applied them to current affairs. His words were brief yet apt, without a single superfluous phrase; his reasoning was lucid and his prose shone with clarity.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾稱為講官第一。

translations.literal: Su Shi called him first among lecture officials.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi ranked him first among lecture officials.

sentences.zh: 祖禹嘗進《唐鑒》十二卷，《帝學》八卷，《仁宗政典》六卷。

translations.literal: Zuyu once presented the Mirror of Tang in twelve scrolls, Imperial Learning in eight scrolls, and Political Canon of Renzong in six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu once presented the Mirror of Tang in twelve scrolls, Imperial Learning in eight scrolls, and the Political Canon of Emperor Renzong in six scrolls.

sentences.zh: 而《唐鑒》深明唐三百年治亂，學者尊之，目為「唐鑒公」云。

translations.literal: The Mirror of Tang deeply clarifies three hundred years of Tang order and chaos; scholars honor it and style him "Lord Mirror of Tang."
translations.idiomatic: The Mirror of Tang brilliantly illuminates three hundred years of Tang order and chaos; scholars revered it and called him "Lord Mirror of Tang."

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，追復龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan he was posthumously restored as Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan he was posthumously restored to the post of Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 子沖，紹興中仕至翰林侍讀學士，《儒林》有傳。

translations.literal: His son Chong, in Shaoxing served up to Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician; the Confucian Forest has his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chong rose during the Shaoxing era to Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician; he has a biography in the Confucian Forest.

sentences.zh: 論曰：熙寧、元豐之際，天下賢士大夫望以為相者，鎮與司馬光二人，至稱之曰君實、景仁，不敢有所軒輊。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: In the Xining and Yuanfeng era, the realm's worthy scholar-officials hoped would become chief councilor were Zhen and Sima Guang—the two men; they even called them by style Junshi and Jingren, not daring any ranking higher or lower.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal states: During the Xining and Yuanfeng eras, the worthy scholar-officials of the realm looked to Fan Zhen and Sima Guang as the men who should become chief councilor; people even addressed them by their styles, Junshi and Jingren, without daring to rank one above the other.

sentences.zh: 光思濟斯民，卒任天下之重；

translations.literal: Guang thought to aid these people and finally bore the realm's heavy burden;
translations.idiomatic: Guang sought to rescue the people and ultimately shouldered the heavy burden of the realm;

sentences.zh: 鎮嶷然如山，確乎其不可拔。

translations.literal: Zhen stood lofty as a mountain, firm and impossible to uproot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen stood lofty as a mountain, steadfast and impossible to move.

sentences.zh: 君子之道，或出或處，易地則皆然，未易以功名優劣論也。

translations.literal: The gentleman's way—sometimes going forth, sometimes remaining—exchanged places and both were so; not easy to judge by achievement and fame as superior or inferior.
translations.idiomatic: The way of the gentleman may lead one into office or into retirement; in the other's place each would have done the same—it is not easy to judge them by the standards of worldly success or failure.

sentences.zh: 百祿受學於鎮，故其議論操修，粹然一出於正。

translations.literal: Bailu received learning from Zhen, therefore his deliberations and conduct were purely all from the upright.
translations.idiomatic: Bailu studied under Zhen, and therefore his opinions and conduct were purely and consistently upright.

sentences.zh: 祖禹長於勸講，平生論諫，不啻數十萬言。

translations.literal: Zuyu excelled at admonitory lecturing; in life his discussions and remonstrances were no less than several hundred thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu excelled at admonitory lecturing; over his lifetime his memorials and remonstrances amounted to no less than several hundred thousand words.

sentences.zh: 其開陳治道，區別邪正，辨釋事宜，平易明白，洞見底蘊，雖賈誼、陸贄不是過云。

translations.literal: His opening and stating the way of governance, distinguishing wicked from upright, explaining and clarifying affairs—plain and clear, penetrating to the foundation—even Jia Yi and Lu Zhi would not surpass it, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In expounding the way of governance, distinguishing the wicked from the upright, and explaining affairs in plain, clear language that penetrated to the root of things, he was said to surpass even Jia Yi and Lu Zhi.
